Read our Privacy notice

Bestselling author Lynda La Plante has been banned from driving for six months, despite her tearful plea to a London court that the disqualification would end her writing career.

The 83-year-old screenwriter and novelist told Lavender Hill Magistrates’ Court her car was essential for meeting criminals and sources, vital for research into her next works of fiction.

Ms La Plante also argued a ban would prevent her from driving her beloved guard dog, Theo, to Roehampton playing fields for walks, a situation she claimed would force her to stop writing altogether.

She stated that if she were unable to transport Theo, she would have to rehome him, adding: "I think the emotional turmoil of that would truly damn my career as a writer."

“It’s very, very solitary, and I work exceptionally hard, and I would just stop.”

La Plante pleaded guilty on Monday to breaking the 20mph speed limit near her home in Kingston-upon-Thames five times between November 2025 and April this year.

open image in gallery La Plante pleaded guilty on Monday to breaking the 20mph speed limit near her home in Kingston-upon-Thames five times between November 2025 and April this year ( PA )

The court heard she already has nine points on her licence, from three speeding offences in June 2023, and June and July 2025.

La Plante, who is best-known for creating Prime Suspect’s no-nonsense detective DCI Jane Tennison, admitted driving at 24mph twice, 25mph, 26mph, and 27mph in the latest offences, which all happened as she took her 18-month-old dog for his daily walk.

Her lawyer Nick Freeman, who is known as Mr Loophole and has represented a string of celebrity clients, urged magistrates to spare her a ban, saying driving is a “vital part of who she is”.

La Plante bluntly told the court she would wind up her writing company if banned, putting four staff members out of work.

But magistrate Mandy Lamplough told the writer she had not done enough to prove that disqualification would cause her “exceptional hardship”.

The magistrates imposed fines totalling £3,330 on La Plante, handed her a six-month ban as her points total rose to 24, and ordered her to pay £130 costs and a £1,332 victim surcharge.

Giving evidence, La Plante said she got her dog Theo after suffering the devastation of the untimely death of another dog, Hugo, who was “in the prime of his life”.

“I don’t want it to sound trivial – this woman and her dog – but I can’t tell you what it was like with this enormous beautiful wolfhound. I don’t know how he did it.

“He would come up into my office, it was as if he said ‘stop’. He knew I had been working for five solid hours, and this paw would come up – bang.”

open image in gallery The magistrates imposed fines totalling £3,330 on La Plante, handed her a six-month ban and ordered her to pay £130 costs and a £1,332 victim surcharge ( Hannah McKay/PA )

Fighting back tears, she said she “lost it” when Hugo died and she “didn’t know what to do with my life”.

And she said her new dog has helped her through the grieving process.

“I love him, it’s as simple as that, but at the same time he has become a great comfort to me,” she said.

La Plante said she drives Theo to be trained on the walk from Roehampton to Wimbledon, and she does not believe nearby Richmond Park is suitable as it is “alive with joggers”, as well as deer, and she is trying to train him not to chase people.

Turning to her writing career, La Plante said she has four books in the works, including one on the Government’s controversial early prison release scheme, and she argued she needed to drive to conduct research interviews.

“If I get a contact who will agree to talk to me, I go to them for research,” she said, setting out how she meets people including criminals in motorway cafes, homeless shelters, prisons, and theatres.

“It’s very difficult when you are meeting forms of criminality, they do like to be very choosy of the location.”

She added that she could not contemplate having a driver, as she would be distracted by questions while trying to recount information on the journey home from her research interviews.

Ahead of her court hearing, La Plante complained about “very confusing” road signs on the A308 in Kingston-upon-Thames, and Mr Freeman suggested she had inadvertently broke the speed limit while concentrating on driving safely.

La Plante, who created hit robbery TV series Widows in the 1980s and brought Prime Suspect to the screen in 1991, was awarded a CBE in 2008 for services to literature, drama and charity.

She was first caught speeding at 9.24am on November 2 last year, when her Toyota was clocked at 24mph on the A308 Kingston Hill.

The second incident happened at 9.35am on March 5, a short distance along the same road, when the author’s car was clocked at 26mph.

In the third offence, she was caught breaking the 20mph limit on April 6 at a speed of 24mph.

She then faced a fourth criminal prosecution, over a speeding offence at 10.03am on April 11 after travelling at 27mph past the same speed camera as the second offence.

The fifth and final offence happened on April 19, when she was driving at 27mph.

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Oil plummets as Trump calls off Iran strikes
News.content:
Oil prices have plunged after Donald Trump called off strikes and said the US and Iran would hold further peace talks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, sank as much as 9.5pc early on Monday to less than $82 a barrel after the US president said he had halted plans for “disastrous” strikes.

Mr Trump said: “Obviously, they don’t want to be attacked. They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon.”

Mr ‌Trump also ordered oil companies to lower petrol prices for American ‌consumers ‌and criticised ⁠Chevron’s chief executive for not crediting his administration for supporting the fossil fuel industry.

The president said that he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on strikes. He halted plans for a major attack against Iran on Saturday, which he said would have been the biggest since the Second World War.

Mr Trump claimed the sides were on the “perimeter” of a peace deal.

Oil’s sharp fall also sent the cost of government borrowing lower on Monday over hopes that it would ease inflation.

The yield on 10-year UK gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, dropped from 5.05pc to 4.98pc, while the equivalent US bonds dropped from 4.74pc to 4.69pc.

Stock markets in Europe also rose, with the FTSE 100 up 0.2pc, the Cac 40 in Paris up 0.3pc and the Dax in Frankfurt climbing 0.1pc.

News.title: Inside the trial for a vaccine to end malaria
News.content:
A small group of brave volunteers were given an experimental vaccine in Oxford this week in a bid to bring to an end the centuries-old scourge of malaria.

“I’m on my second vaccine now. Then I’m due to have my third vaccine soon, and then in November, I’ll be given malaria,” said an upbeat Mike Luciw, a 32-year-old local who works in recruitment.

“The hope is to help find something that could save millions of people.”

There are already two licenced vaccines for malaria but the new Oxford “RH5” shot is not like anything that has come before.

The existing jabs only act against malaria as it moves towards the liver in the early stage of infection, and provide only partial protection.

The new combination vaccine, in contrast, is designed to fight it off both at the liver stage and in the wider bloodstream, effectively knocking it out altogether.

The project is being run by the husband and wife team of Simon Draper, Professor of Vaccinology and Translational Medicine at the University of Oxford, and Professor Angela Minassian, an infectious disease specialist and clinical lead for their malaria programme in Oxford’s Department of Paediatrics.

“The dream for malaria … has been to have these two lines of defence, liver and blood, so if the first line fails, you’ve got a second,” says Prof Draper, who leads on the science.

“Our dream is to have a vaccine that gives over 90 per cent efficacy in African children,” adds Prof Minassian, who heads the clinical trials for the new jab.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Josh Kerr turns ‘race of the century’ into one-sided show of power
News.content:
“It means everything – absolutely incredible,” said Kerr, who joined the rendition of Flower of Scotland before closing his eyes to soak up the moment in a stadium where he had competed as a child in even the shot put.

“To do it in front of a Scottish crowd, where I learned how to race, doesn’t get any better,” he added. “I came here week after week growing up as a kid. This was the championship of my season with the world indoors and going after the record. This was on the calendar before any of that. I think a British crowd deserved more from me and I owed them that.”

Of the tactics compared to his world record, where he had to hold an even pace throughout, Kerr stressed the importance of staying calm and not being tempted into pushing too soon. “London was a big stress, pushing my body to the extreme limit,” he said. “Doing a championship race is a nice clean slate; using your brain instead of your body. It’s how I love to race.

“When you’re running that slow, your job is not to waste energy and I did that. I knew an opportunity would open up. Then it was about staying awake and alive and trying to get some space. felt like I had plenty of gears left in me.”

Kerr had emerged to a huge home ovation and, with the Proclaimers booming out as the runners completed the first two laps, he was content to stay in the pack even as Myers followed. There was then only one brief moment of concern as the runners began gathering themselves during the penultimate lap and Kerr became momentarily boxed in.

News.title: Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid
News.content:
Manchester United 2 Atletico Madrid 1

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal saga has Newcastle in contention for all-time worst transfer window
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal saga has Newcastle in contention for all-time worst transfer window

Newcastle's chief executive stated a desire to be amongst the best clubs in the world in four years - but a transfer window that has seen their best players leave and their captain wanting out is putting that ambition in question

View 3 Images Newcastle are desperate to keep hold of Bruno Guimaraes as they try to avoid a disaster summer (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Bruno Guimaraes has reported for Newcastle's pre-season camp as talk over his sale continues - and his possible exit would make their summer go from bad to worse.

‌



The Magpies are currently fighting to keep their captain after two high-profile sales at St James' Park and the departure of their manager.

‌



So often poor transfer windows centre around dire recruitment, the expensive signings who fail to work out. But in terms of exits we could certainly be looking at one of the worst summers in the history of the Premier League.

‌



There's no doubt that the hangover from the poor summer of 12 months ago, which centred around Alexander Isak's desire to leave, eventually joining Liverpool on deadline day, has bled into the window we're currently in.

Newcastle's forgettable summer of 2025 set them on a path to a first bottom-half finish in recent years, and that had financial consequences which has seen players jump ship. The ripples are certainly being felt.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Arsenal target Bruno Guimaraes complies with Newcastle requests as midfielder boards flight READ MORE :

Arsenal receive immediate response after finally submitting first Bruno Guimaraes offer READ MORE :

Anthony Gordon's move to Barcelona can be written off as the one major deal that Newcastle were always going to have to sanction to remain financially compliant, especially after they missed out on European revenue. The £70million deal was one the majority could stomach.

Sandro Tonali's £100m switch to Tottenham is one that the balance sheet can live with, but what it says to the rest of the squad is perhaps more damaging than the exit itself. The Italian had been linked with Arsenal in January and given that Newcastle nearly doubled their money on the £55m they spent on him, you think fair play.

The issue is the likes of Guimaraes, who with Tonali alongside formed a midfield partnership that could genuinely be compared to any side in the Premier League. That was the only area where the Magpies could claim they were in the elite bracket, and that's a great foundation to build from.

‌



Instead it could implode. Tonali's departure doesn't send a message of ambition and Guimaraes has expressed a desire to move to Arsenal. Newcastle have stood firm, maintaining their talisman is not for sale.

View 3 Images Sandro Tonali joined Tottenham in a club-record deal (Image: Tottenham Hotspur FC)

The Brazilian's exit would leave Newcastle, entering a new era under Matthias Jaissle, looking more and more like a mid-table side. A number of their blockbuster arrivals under the Saudi Arabian regime will have moved on, and questioned will be asked of the project.

‌



Manchester United continue to track left-back Lewis Hall, who has just enjoyed the best season of his career to date. If Guimaraes were to be sold then Newcastle would be financially able to rebuff any offer that comes in for Hall - and they insist he's not for sale.

Even so, the player's head may well be turned, and a squad full of players who would rather be elsewhere isn't a recipe for success. Newcastle were quick to land a new manager, but he's an uphill task ahead of him.

Much has been made of Newcastle's failure to get deals over the line. James Trafford, Marc Guehi, Hugo Ekitike, Joao Pedro and Bryan Mbeumo have all opted for other Premier League rivals ahead of the Magpies.

‌



View 3 Images Eddie Howe has called time on five years at Newcastle (Image: PA)

Missing out on those names has certainly halted Newcastle's progress, but being able to retain their best players has meant that Howe, when he was in situ, had enough to work with that he could challenge England's best on their day. Consistency remained the problem, but a squad boasting Tonali, Guimaraes and Isak was able to end the club's 70-year wait for a trophy.

That was only 18 months ago and yet it seems like that was in a different era such has been the shift in the way many see Newcastle, even those within their four walls.

‌



Its not to say the club haven't spent money - upwards of £100m has been spent of summer arrivals that include Ewen Jaouen, Bazoumana Toure and Sean Steur. But the fact their signings have done nothing to mitigate the negative feeling around Newcastle says everything about the magnitude of the players they've let go - and those that could still follow them.

Only last year new chief executive David Hopkinson claimed Newcastle can be “in the debate about being the top club in the world ” by 2030. Make no mistake, four years out from that goal, no club sanctions the type of exits that the Magpies have without heavyweight names coming in to replace them.

Sports.title: Man Utd tell Ralf Rangnick's only signing he can leave permanently after brutal snub
Sports.content:
Man Utd tell Ralf Rangnick's only signing he can leave permanently after brutal snub

Ralf Rangnick could not impart many changes during his fleeting spell as manager of Manchester United, but even one of those is seemingly being rooted out of the club

View 3 Images Ralf Rangnick's only Man United signing has been told he can leave the club this summer (Image: 2022 Manchester United FC)

Ralf Rangnick's only transfer signing as interim manager of Manchester United has been told he is allowed to leave the club. Rangnick took over the Reds on a temporary basis after Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was sacked during the 2021-22 Premier League campaign.

‌



The Austrian was in charge during the following transfer window and while the club were linked with many players recommended by him, only one was brought to the club. That player was Toby Collyer, who arrived from Brighton and Hove Albion as an 18-year-old prospect.

‌



Four-and-a-half years later, Collyer has reportedly been informed he is allowed to depart the club permanently, having been left out of Michael Carrick's squad for the recent friendly over Atletico Madrid. His absence would have stung as the substitutes' bench was filled with plenty of young academy stars.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Instead, Collyer featured for the U21s side in a 1-0 defeat to Altrincham Town on Friday evening. Last season, Collyer was loaned to Championship side West Bromwich Albion, before being loaned to Hull City in the following transfer window.

Throughout his time at the club, he has only made 13 senior appearances for the Reds, with ten of those coming under Ruben Amorim. His loan spells with West Brom and Hull were both marred by injuries. Now, according to The Sun, the club have said he is free to leave.

‌



Despite United starting the summer short in central midfield, Collyer always seemed far away from Carrick's plans. They have since strengthened by signing Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos from Aston Villa and Chelsea respectively.

View 3 Images Toby Collyer featured against Altrincham Town when many other United youngsters were included in the squad against Atletico Madrid (Image: 2026 Manchester United FC)

A third midfielder is also expected to be brought in this summer. Meanwhile, fellow academy graduate Tyler Fletcher is believed to be ahead of the ex-Brighton prospect in the United pecking order.

‌



Against Altrincham, he was joined by fellow United U21 team-mates Dan Gore, Jacob Devaney and Chido Obi, who all featured in the friendlies against Wrexham and Rosenborg.

Collyer's loan spell with West Brom came to an end after he suffered an injury during a clash against Birmingham City towards the end of November. He was brought back to United to work on his recovery, before being loaned to Hull.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick has made many big changes at Manchester United since taking over from Ruben Amorim (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

‌



He hoped to be involved in Hull's promotion play-off final clash against Middlesbrough at Wembley but he could not recover from his injury in time. He made 12 appearances for West Brom before the loan was ended and he only made five at Hull.

Collyer's departure would also rip out the last bit of Rangnick's legacy at Old Trafford. The now Austria manager took charge of 29 matches, winning 11, drawing nine and losing nine.

He had been expected to take up a consultancy role at Old Trafford, but this did not transpire as he left the club completely upon the end of his caretaker deal.

Sports.title: Kevin Keegan's 'overwhelmed' family issue heartfelt statement and explain funeral plans
Sports.content:
Kevin Keegan's 'overwhelmed' family issue heartfelt statement and explain funeral plans

Kevin Keegan died on July 20 following a battle with stomach cancer and his family have now issued a statement to thank those who paid tribute and detail plans for his funeral

View 3 Images Kevin Keegan died aged 75 from cancer (Image: (Liverpool FC via Getty Images))

Kevin Keegan's family say they have been "truly overwhelmed" by the volume of tributes following the death of the football legend. England great Keegan passed away aged 75 last month from cancer.

‌



It was announced on July 20 that the former Liverpool, Hamburg, Southampton and Newcastle striker had died following a battle with stomach cancer. The Newcastle hero left behind wife of 51 years Jean and their children Laura Jane, 47, and Sarah Marie, 43.

‌



Tributes poured in from across the heartbroken football world for the double Ballon d'Or winner, who won 63 caps for England and managed the Three Lions, Newcastle, Fulham and Manchester City.

‌



A private funeral has now been arranged by the Keegan family, who have also set up a fundraiser in King Kev's honour, which will raise money for charities close to his heart.

Gianni Infantino's opponents prepared to launch rival competition to force out FIFA boss READ MORE :

Southampton boss Tonda Eckert says he received death threats after Spygate scandal READ MORE :

A statement from the Keegan family, issued by the League Managers Association, read: “Following the devastating news of Kevin’s passing, we would like to thank the vast number of people who have expressed condolences and shared their memories of Kevin in recent days.

“As a family we have been truly overwhelmed by the volume of tributes and are grateful for them all. We will be holding a small private funeral in the coming weeks and request ongoing privacy and respect whilst we navigate this extremely difficult period as a family.

‌



“Details of a memorial service hosted by Newcastle United that will take place at a later date will be communicated in due course.”

The fundraiser states: "The Keegan family are deeply grateful for all the kind words and support received from far and wide. To honour Kevin’s memory, they feel there would be no more fitting gesture than to give.

View 3 Images Kevin Keegan touched the hearts of many

‌



"We are therefore raising money for two causes that were close to Kevin’s heart: The Christie Charity and Football Families for Justice. The Christie were an immeasurable help to Kevin and his family, as they are to many others. Football Families for Justice is a charity being set-up by John Stiles, son of the great Nobby Stiles, to support former players who are suffering from neuro degenerative diseases caused by heading the ball during their football career.

"A sporting superstar, but also a husband, father, grandfather and friend - Kevin gave so much to us all."

Keegan was most loved at Newcastle, where he enjoyed his most successful spell as a manager. "Kevin was more than a legendary footballer and manager. He was the beating heart of Newcastle United for generations of supporters," the club said in a statement.

‌



View 3 Images Kevin Keegan was a legend at Newcastle United (Image: PA)

"As a player, he brought world-class talent, ambition and belief to St. James’ Park, helping to transform perceptions of what Newcastle United could be. As a manager, he ignited our city. Kevin gave supporters hope and pride, and led a team whose style, spirit and passion captured the imagination of football fans around the world. He was so much more than an Entertainer.

"Kevin forged an extraordinary bond with Newcastle, built on the roots of his father, Joe. He understood our people. He embraced the North East with a passion that was genuine and unwavering, and in return, he earned his rightful place in the hearts of millions."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino's opponents prepared to launch rival competition to force out FIFA boss
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino's opponents prepared to launch rival competition to force out FIFA boss

FIFA president Gianni Infantino is holding on by his finger nails, but his opponents are trying to get rid of him and are ready to take extreme steps to ensure that he is ousted

View 2 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino said the proposal will not proceed (Image: VCG via Getty Images)

The leaders of UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC are ready to take extreme measures to oust FIFA boss Gianni Infantino - which includes setting up their own rival competition.

‌



The days of the FIFA president appear numbered in the wake of his failed plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup, but Infantino is determined to fight on. He's tried to lean on old acquaintances, but he's lost the faith of several of the world's major organisations.

‌



UEFA have been the most outspoken federation and have backing from other continental organisations. The Times reports that they're prepared to create their own tournament and UEFA have a blueprint for a global league having commissioned one in 2017, without using it.

‌



One source told the newspaper: “Everyone is very determined he needs to go, and if not we will take all the necessary steps [to remove him from power]. That includes future international competitions — would the big South American countries prefer to play France or Spain, or Lebanon or Djibouti? Everyone is very determined, there are no backward steps now.”

FA chiefs should be embarrassed by their prior support of disgraced Gianni Infantino READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump meeting not happening as third nation calls out FIFA boss READ MORE :

It remains feasible that Infantino will ignore the noise and try for re-election in March as he eyes a fourth term. Infantino’s opponents would therefore be prepared to impose a “governance boycott” which would see them refuse to take part in FIFA council or committee meetings.

A number of European associations, including England and Wales, have withdrawn letters of support for Infantino’s re-election after his World Cup sale plans fell flat. It comes after the FA had supported Infantino via a letter as recently as June.

‌



UEFA were outspoken against the FIFA president during the World Cup, heavily criticising his decision to suspended the red card handed to Folarin Balogun whilst their president Aleksander Ceferin refused to attend the final last month in New York.

View 2 Images UEFA strongly opposed FIFA's plans and want rid of Gianni Infantino (Image: Harry Murphy/UEFA via Getty Images)

Europe's governing body has signalled its intent to take legal action after FIFA and said in a letter: “UEFA hereby gives formal notice that it is actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints arising out of and in connection with the FFE plan proposed by Fifa and all related matters.

Article continues below

“You and Fifa are required to take immediate steps to identify, locate, and preserve all documents and electronically stored information described in this notice that are in your or Fifa’s possession, custody, or control.

“These obligations arise independently of any internal retention policy you or your organisation maintain and supersede any routine document destruction or deletion policies that would otherwise apply.”

Sports.title: Liverpool set for major cash injection as club enter advanced talks after £324m reveal
Sports.content:
Liverpool set for major cash injection as club enter advanced talks after £324m reveal

Liverpool are "working hard behind the scenes" and "pretty advanced in terms of speaking to the right people" ahead of this coming Premier League season starting

View 2 Images Liverpool could become the first Premier League club to expand their retail stores into the United States (Image: Carl Recine, Getty Images)

Liverpool are said to be in advanced talks to open permanent retail stores in the United States. No Premier League club has yet to launch any physical shops Stateside, with Manchester City coming closest, but only previously running pop-ups.

‌



Paris Saint-Germain are the pioneers in this regard across European football, opening their first store in Los Angeles five years ago and have since opened two more in Miami and New York City. The latter is their largest outside of France.

‌



PSG even expanded their presence on Fifth Avenue within 18 months. Liverpool now appear next in line to make the move.

‌



Liverpool handed Bradley Barcola transfer boost as PSG strike contingency plan READ MORE :

Liverpool transfer need brutally exposed as Leeds stun Andoni Iraola - 5 talking points READ MORE :

Liverpool's chief commercial officer Ben Latty told Sportico of Liverpool's ongoing discussions: "Clearly, we're not at the end of that because we haven't opened anything or announced anything yet, but I'd say we are pretty advanced in terms of speaking to the right people."

Liverpool have launched stores in Bali and London in recent months, with existing outlets already operating in Denmark, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Ireland, Singapore, South Africa and the United Kingdom.

The club's chief commercial officer is reportedly hopeful that their current tally of 26 stores will surpass 30 before the end of this season. Latty added: "We can't expect our numbers to grow organically.

‌



"We've got to work for them, and we've got to strategically put our investment where we think it's going to return the highest revenue for us as a club, so yeah, we are working hard behind the scenes."

View 2 Images Liverpool chief executive Billy Hogan spoke earlier this summer about the United States' importance (Image: John Powell, Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Liverpool's most recent accounts, filed for the 2024-25 campaign, reveal that their commercial income stood at £324million. Only City (£340million) and Manchester United (£333million) posted higher figures amongst Premier League sides.

‌



Speaking while part of this summer's fortnight-long pre-season tour, where the squad was stationed in Chicago, chief executive Billy Hogan said: "The US is a really important market from our perspective.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"A huge fan base here, over 26 million supporters of the club, which, I'm told, actually, the only US sports team that has more fans is the LA Lakers. So, a pretty good indication of the popularity of the club.

‌



"It's our number one international retail market. We are the number two most-watched team in European football here in the US. So, the team is incredibly popular.

"It's an important market from our perspective. (Almost 40 per cent) of our partners are here. And so, all of that kind of comes together to make it a super-important market from our perspective."

Sports.title: FA chiefs should be embarrassed by their prior support of disgraced Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
The Football Association will write a letter revoking its endorsement of Gianni Infantino’s re-election. To which there is one obvious reaction. Why on earth did they ever endorse him?

There will be - there should be - some shamed faces in the FA’s executive ranks right now. The photograph of the FA chair presenting Infantino with a personalised England shirt during the World Cup is not one Debbie Hewitt will want to see again.

But there has been a long line of FA chairs and chief executives who have been happy to go along with Infantino’s regime. In theory, the FA should have one of the most powerful voices in world football but, effectively, it has been silent during a decade in which his tenure has become increasingly embarrassing.

Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump meeting not happening as third nation calls out FIFA boss READ MORE :

The FA’s endorsement of Infantino came after he had turned World Cup football into a game of four quarters. It came after he had given Donald Trump a ‘peace prize’ on behalf of FIFA.

‌



It came after he had somehow managed to allow Saudi Arabia to be unopposed as hosts of the 2034 World Cup. It came after he had sanctioned the outrageous prices most had to pay for World Cup tickets. It came after THAT half-time show.

The FA should never have endorsed his re-election in the first place. They were not alone, of course.

In fact, it appeared there was only going to be the possibility of one or two dissenters when it came to the formality of re-electing Infantino. Now, of course, any possibility of Infantino being re-elected has been blown out of the water.

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino gave Donald Trump the FIFA Peace Prize in December (Image: PA)

‌



In terms of revoking endorsement, the Welsh set the ball rolling when it released a statement on Monday morning. It read: “The Football Association of Wales hereby confirms its withdrawal of support for the candidature of Mr Gianni Infantino for re-election as FIFA president for the 2027-31 term.

“The recent failures in good governance, processes, leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgement have led us to a position where Mr Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to remain at the helm of world football. Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.”

Again, the obvious response is to wonder how he had their confidence in the first place. Nevertheless, the withdrawal of endorsements - while largely symbolic - should confirm this is the end for Infantino’s reign.

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino has no way back at FIFA (Image: Getty Images)

‌



UEFA have even written to him, demanding no paperwork relating to the scheme - which would have seen FIFA sell rights to the World Cup to private investors - is destroyed and reserving the right to take legal action. The Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, has called on his to step down.

As it still stands, Infantino plans to stand for re-election at a congress in Morocco in March and would need 106 votes from the 211 member nations to stay in his job.

But with UEFA and CONCACAF already releasing strong statements criticising his leadership, the chances of Infantino’s time in charge of FIFA being extended are extremely slim. In fact, they are surely non-existent.

Sports.title: Nygren spares Hogh blushes as Celtic begin title defence with win
Sports.content:
Celtic made a winning start to their Scottish Premiership title defence with a 1-0 victory over battling Dundee at Celtic Park.

After Rangers had been held by Dundee United on Friday night and Hearts were beaten at Aberdeen on Saturday, Celtic capitalised on opening-round slip-ups from their rivals thanks to Benjamin Nygren's second-half header.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Benjamin Nygren scores Celtic's first goal of the season with a header from a great cross from Kieran Tierney to give the home side the lead against Dundee

It wasn't all plain sailing though, with goalkeeper Viljami Sinisalo required to make a super stop to prevent Dundee sub Ashley Hay heading in a late leveller.

Martin O'Neill's side should have been out of sight by then but had seen club-record £11m signing Kasper Hogh spurn two good opportunities inside the first 13 minutes. He then blew a third good chance of the night on 85 minutes, shooting wide from close range before captain Callum McGregor pinged a right-foot shot against a post.

While Hogh laboured, fellow new attacker Camilo Duran looked lively cutting in from the right but it was last season's top scorer Nygren who came up with the crucial moment from Kieran Tierney's fine cross.

Image: GLASGOW, SCOTLAND - AUGUST 03: Celtic's Benjamin Nygren celebrates scoring to make it 1-0 during a William Hill Premiership match between Celtic and Dundee at Celtic Park, on August 03, 2026, in Glasgow, Scotland. (Photo by Craig Williamson / SNS G

Dundee boss Steven Pressley had called on his side to be "positive" at the home of the champions and his side were certainly that, with Charlie Reilly clipping the side-netting in a good first half from the visitors and on another night they could have profited from their 11 shots and Celtic's wastefulness.

Celtic's need to strengthen their squad further this summer is clear and they will need to find some more sharpness before the key Champions League qualifier against LASK in two-and-a-half weeks' time. But, unlike their title rivals, they are up and running with three points.

More to follow...

The key moments from Celtic Park

9: MISS! A misplaced pass at the back from Dundee sees Kasper Hogh played into the box - but he skews his shot badly wide of the near post. "That's an awful finish," said Chris Sutton on co-commentary.

13: MISS! Hogh is off target again, failing to divert Benjamin Nygren's shot into the bottom corner.

15: SIDE-NETTING! Charlie Reilly clips the side-netting with Dundee's first shot of the game.

34: SHOT! Owen Bevan has Dundee's first shot on target - but it's an easy stop for Viljami Sinisalo.

38: WIDE! Arne Engels looks primed to head Celtic in front but nods his effort the wrong side of the post.

41: SAVE! Kieran Tierney bursts into the box but his drilled shot is well saved by Owen Goodman - Celtic's first shot on target at the 10th attempt.

52: GOAL! Tierney swings in a cross for Nygren to head in the opener from close range.

67: SAVE! Hyun-Jun Yang strikes from 30 yards but Goodman gets down well to make the save.

82: BIG SAVE! Sinisalo does brilliantly to get down to his right to get a hand to Ashley Hay's header which was going towards the bottom corner.

85: ANOTHER MISS FOR HOGH! Hogh passes up his third good chance of the night, stabbing a close-range shot wide of the post.

85: OFF THE POST! Callum McGregor drives into the D and bends a right-foot shot at goal but the ball pings back off the post.

What the result means and what's next...

Sports.title: Serena to resume comeback alongside sister Venus in Cincinnati
Sports.content:
Serena and Venus Williams are set to play at the Cincinnati Open after being awarded a wild card for the women's doubles draw.

Serena made a sensational return to tennis during the grass-court season after almost four years out of the professional game, but the 44-year-old suffered a knee injury during a first-round singles loss which led to her and Venus withdrawing from the doubles at the All England Club.

Serena played doubles in London at Queen's Club and at the Berlin Open - but not alongside Venus on either occasion - as she prepared for Wimbledon.

Venus, who turned 46 in June, has also been given a wild card for the singles draw in Cincinnati. She is seeking a first singles victory of 2026 having lost in the first round of all eight of the tournaments she has entered this year.

Venus has had slightly more success playing doubles in 2026, claiming a sole victory at two of the six tournaments she has entered. She most recently played alongside Britain's Katie Boulter in Madrid and breakout star Alexandra Eala in Berlin.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Judy Murray discusses Serena Williams' comeback to tennis.

Among the other players to be awarded singles wild cards for the tournament were fellow Americans Sloane Stephens and Taylor Townsend.

As a doubles pairing, the Williams sisters have won 14 Major titles and three Olympic gold medals. They last took the court for a doubles match together at the 2022 US Open and will be playing the Cincinnati Open for the first time as a team.

Sports.title: Graham stars as Welsh Fire upset Southern Brave in last-ball thriller
Sports.content:
Welsh Fire turned the form table on its head to defeat The Hundred table-toppers Southern Brave in a last-ball thriller in Cardiff.

Until the last dozen deliveries, it looked like it was to be rinse and repeat for the visitors, putting up what seemed a below-par total before unleashing their formidable bowling attack to squeeze the opposition to defeat - but brilliant cameos from Heather Graham and Niamh Holland at the death saw Fire triumph in an absolute thriller to keep their hopes alive.

Having lost their last two games in addition to being hampered by the loss of their captain Sophie Devine - ruled out of the tournament with a calf injury - Welsh Fire desperately needed a win against the unbeaten league-leaders.

In their previous five wins, Brave had twice defended 126-7 and 140-3, and chased 115 and 117. They are curiously the only team in the men's or women's competition not to have gone past 140.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lizelle Lee looked to have lost control of the ball but regained her composure just in time to stump Ella McCaughan.

Today, their batting misfired again after Sophie Molineux became the first captain to win the toss and bat in this year's women's tournament.

The openers were gone after 16 balls, and Laura Wolvaardt and Jemimah Rodrigues rebuilt in uncharacteristically pedestrian style. Batting was not easy on a turning pitch, and the Brave stumbled to 121-5, Welsh Fire seemingly on top but aware of Brave's bowling threat.

Georgia Voll went past Sophia Dunkley to become the 2026 competition's leading run-scorer but departed for 11 to Tilly Corteen-Coleman's second ball, with young spinner having Ella McCaughan stumped from her fifth.

And when the economical Issy Wong hit Devine's replacement Orla Prendergast's stumps, Brave were squeezing the opposition in habitual style, despite bowling an unusual number of wides.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sarah Glenn takes a great catch to get the first wicket of the innings.

A Lauren Bell slower ball deceived Wareham to leave Fire in real trouble, needing 52 off 38 but an unexpected six-four combo from debutant Grace Thompson, in for Em Arlott, put the cat amongst the pigeons. She was then caught, and it looked like the nous and skills of Molineux and Bell would see Brave home.

But that was to reckon without another young talent in Holland. She swept and drove boundaries to leave three runs needed off two, then Lee should have run Graham out but dropped the ball to leave a single needed off the last ball. And Graham gleefully hit Bell through the infield to spark the celebrations.

Match Hero Graham said: "For Niamh to come in at the end, run really well with me, and get a few boundaries away herself; the win is more for those guys than me. It's always nerve-wracking in situations like that. I've played for a lot of years now and been in plenty of tight games, so you just rely on those past experiences to help get you over the line."

What's next in The Hundred?

The Hundred continues on Tuesday with SunRisers Leeds hosting London Spirit at Headingley. The women's fixture begins at 3pm, with the men's contest following at 6.30pm.

Sports.title: Eala beats Pegula at DC Open to claim first WTA Tour title
Sports.content:
Rising Filipina star Alexandra Eala came from a set down against Jessica Pegula to claim the first WTA Tour singles title of her career at the DC Open.

Eala had trailed by a set when the match was suspended because of heavy rain on Sunday, but the 21-year-old turned the contest round on Monday to claim a 4-6 6-4 6-0 victory.

The victory made Eala the first Filipina to win a singles title on the tour, completing the same career-defining breakthrough that the Washington tournament once gave Pegula when she claimed her first WTA Tour title in 2019.

Eala's popularity soared during the grass-court season as she beat some of the sport's biggest names on runs to the semi-finals in Berlin and last 16 at Wimbledon.

She has swiftly become a huge star in the Philippines, and the nation's flags were dotted throughout the Stadium Court in Washington as chants for Eala routinely outweighed those for Pegula.

It capped a week in which the rising star transformed the atmosphere around the tournament while reaching her first WTA Tour final in her debut at the hard-court tune-up for the US Open.

The two traded breaks midway through the opening set, with Pegula breaking again at 4-4 and serving out the set at love. The players held through the opening three games of the second set before heavy rain suspended play on Sunday afternoon, with Eala up 2-1.

When they returned on Monday, the momentum belonged to Eala. She stormed back to claim the second set, then swept through the third.

She won each game of the final set of the match to complete the comeback in an hour and 47 minutes of court time.

In the process, she defeated all three of the tournament's top seeds and turned the biggest week of her career into a historic first title.

Sports.title: Raducanu to miss US Open
Sports.content:
Emma Raducanu's stress fracture will force her to miss the US Open.

The British No 1 suffered the injury to her right lower leg during the grass-court season and made a late decision to pull out of Wimbledon.

According to the Press Association, following consultation with her medical team, Raducanu has concluded she will be unable to play in New York later this month.

While the news comes as no surprise given the nature of the injury and the fact Raducanu has only recently taken her first tentative steps back on court wearing a protective boot, it is another blow to the 23-year-old.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hours before withdrawing from Wimbledon, Emma Raducanu told the media that she intended to compete despite pushing beyond anything she normally would.

Having made positive progress last summer, including winning her first matches at Flushing Meadows since lifting the trophy five years ago, it has been a frustrating 12 months for Raducanu with more persistent physical issues.

After a foot injury severely hampered her pre-season training, Raducanu then spent two-and-a-half months off court with a post-viral illness after initially falling unwell in early February.

She finally returned for the end of the clay-court season having rehired Andrew Richardson, the coach who guided her to the US Open title, but the pair's time on court together has been limited.

Sports.title: Maguire handed Solheim Cup return as Europe's captain's picks revealed
Sports.content:
Leona Maguire has been included among Team Europe's captain's picks for next month's Solheim Cup, with Anna Nordqvist adding three more rookies to her line-up.

Maguire has featured in the last three Solheim Cups, top-scoring as an unbeaten rookie in Europe's away win over Team USA in 2021 before making further appearances in 2023 and 2024.

The 31-year-old was the highest-ranked European player in the Rolex Women's World Golf Rankings not to qualify automatically, having posted three top-10 finishes on the LPGA Tour this season but missed the cut in four of the five majors.

Image: Leona Maguire has won 8.5 points for Team Europe from 12 matches during her three previous appearances

Maguire was the only player with past Solheim Cup experience named among Nordqvist's picks, announced live on Sky Sports, with Spain's Julia Lopez Ramirez, France's Nastasia Nadaud and England's Mimi Rhodes the other selections.

Image: Team Europe's confirmed 12-player line-up for this year's Solheim Cup

"I'm really excited to be part of Team Europe again in September," Maguire said. "I love the Solheim Cup, it brings the best out of my game and I love being part of the team."

It leaves Team Europe with four debutants in their line-up to face Angela Stanford's Team USA at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands from September 11-13, where the hosts look to regain the trophy after their 2024 loss.

Sports.title: More European countries withdraw support for Infantino as pressure intensifies
Sports.content:
European countries began turning their backs on Gianni Infantino as moves intensified across the globe to end his crisis-hit tenure as Fifa president.

The Football Association was the highest-profile of several Uefa member associations to drop its support for Infantino’s proposed re-election next year. It will write to Fifa confirming it no longer endorses Infantino for a fourth term in charge after the intense controversy surrounding his failed plan to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors.

Wales and Serbia publicly confirmed that they had withdrawn their backing, following a lead taken by Finland last week. Along with the FA, those federations had all previously written letters in favour of Infantino prolonging his tenure but patience has run out across the continent. The Swedish Football Association, which was one of five European FAs not to write letters of support, issued a statement confirming it would oppose his candidature in the election in March.

The FA had previously fallen into line behind Infantino, who will helm an extraordinary Fifa congress confirming the United Kingdom’s hosting of the 2035 Women’s World Cup in November if he is still in position. But it has been consistent in condemning his doomed Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, publicly and in private representations. On Saturday it called for a “full and robust review of Fifa’s leadership and governance”, and its latest move is a further escalation.

It is joined by the Football Association of Wales, which said in a statement: “The Football Association of Wales hereby confirms its withdrawal of support for the candidature of Mr Gianni Infantino for re-election as Fifa president for the 2027-2031 term.

“The recent failures in good governance, processes, leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgment have led us to a position where Mr Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to remain at the helm of world football. Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.”

Striking a similar tone, the Football Association of Serbia explained recent events had “seriously damaged the reputation and credibility of both Fifa and its president”, saying a withdrawal was “the only logical and rational step”.

In a sign that consensus may not be easy to achieve, the Swiss Football Association stopped short of abandoning its countryman. Instead it asked for “another personal exchange of views with the Fifa president” and said it would “continue to review the developments surrounding Fifa” before the leadership election.

More countries are, however, expected to withdraw their support for Infantino in what amounts to a vote of no confidence. The intended effect is for the embattled president to resign although some insiders are braced for a drawn-out process. While the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and Concacaf, which runs the sport in North and Central America, have both strongly criticised Infantino there has been no move by any of their individual federations to call back letters in favour of his re-election.

Ensuring they do so may be critical to the ongoing efforts to remove Infantino quickly. There is acknowledgement in some parts of Europe that other continents should be seen taking the lead if enough of a groundswell for his departure is to be reached. Only 15 countries have publicly supported Infantino since he shelved the FFE project on Saturday but there is an appetite to form a broad coalition against his re-election quickly.

The Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, is a contender to take over if Infantino is deposed. Montagliani is understood to be in consensus with the Uefa and AFC hierarchies that new leadership is needed at Fifa.

In another blow to Infantino, lawyers acting for Uefa have ordered him and other staff to identify, locate and preserve all documents related to the FFE scheme. Their letter includes Arsène Wenger, the Fifa chief of global football development, among those obliged to comply with its order. It says Uefa is “actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints ... arising out of and in connection with the FFE plan”.

Thrive Eternal, the investment firm that had been expected to lead a group taking a 20% stake in FFE, is believed to have been sent a similar letter. JP Morgan, which was enlisted for an advisory role in the scheme, is also understood to have received an order related to FFE.

On Monday afternoon the US State Department denied reports that Infantino had been scheduled to meet Marco Rubio, the United States secretary of state, in a bid to stoke up support for his continued reign as president.

Sports.title: Charlton up for sale again as US owners look to cash in after three years
Sports.content:
Charlton’s US owners have put the club up for sale just three years after taking over at the Valley. The ownership group is understood to have engaged Oakwell Sports Advisory to find what would be the club’s fifth owners in the past six years.

In a sales deck sent to potential investors, which has been seen by the Guardian, Oakwell describes Charlton as “the last remaining football club upside opportunity in London”. Oakwell also claims that Charlton would provide new owners with an opportunity for five to 10 times equity growth through promotion to the Premier League, commercial expansion and investment in women’s football.

Oakwell did the deal that led to the Bournemouth owner, Bill Foley, buying the Prem rugby club Exeter Chiefs this summer, and is helping the Rugby Football League to secure external investment, but has little recent history of completing football transactions.

Charlton’s location in south-east London is a plus, while the Valley is a modern stadium with a capacity of 27,000, but the club do not own the ground, which belongs to the hated former owner Roland Duchâtelet. Having considered looking at alternative sites, last year Charlton extended the lease on the Valley until 2040.

Charlton have repeatedly changed hands since the fans forced out Duchâtelet in 2020, when the club had three owners in quick succession. Duchâtelet sold Charlton to East Street Investments for just £1 in January 2020, but the consortium led initially by the former football agent Matt Southall collapsed amid in‑fighting and an acrimonious court case, with the club eventually bought by the Danish-American business Thomas Sandgaard later that year. In 2023, Sandgaard sold Charlton to a group of five US investors called Global Football Partners (GFP) led by Gabriel Brener via their UK subsidiary, SE7 Partners.

Under GFP, Charlton returned to the Championship for the first time in five years in 2025 by winning the League One playoff final at Wembley, while the women’s team were promoted to WSL1 last season.

GFP paid around £15m for Charlton three years ago but, having invested in the stadium and training ground and seen Nathan Jones’s side consolidate the club in the Championship, will be looking for several times that figure. Charlton declined to comment.

Sports.title: Newcastle reject first bid from Arsenal for captain Bruno Guimarães
Sports.content:
Arsenal have stepped up their attempt to sign Bruno Guimarães by finally beginning formal transfer negotiations and making an opening offer, which Newcastle have rejected.

Guimarães met Newcastle’s incoming manager, Matthias Jaissle, for the first time on Monday at the team’s pre-season training camp at La Manga after a post-World Cup holiday in Brazil.

There had been suggestions that the 28-year-old midfielder would fly to London for a medical at Arsenal, but instead he boarded a commercial flight to Spain.

Once at La Manga, he was expected to tell Jaissle of his determination to swap Tyneside for north London, but everything hinges on whether Arsenal are prepared to meet Newcastle’s valuation for a player with two years remaining on his contract.

While executives at Arsenal believe Guimarães is worth a maximum of £70m – and a bid in that ballpark was rejected on Monday – Newcastle value their captain at around £80m.

If some sort of compromise seems likely given Arsenal – negotiating, initially, through intermediaries – have spent much of this summer in pursuit of a midfielder at the top of Mikel Arteta’s shopping list, Newcastle are under no pressure to sell.

View image in fullscreen Guimarães has had several battles with Arsenal over the past few seasons. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters

Indeed, having sold Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali to Barcelona and Tottenham respectively this summer, they would prefer to offer Jaissle the benefit of Guimarães’s talent and experience as he rebuilds the squad.

The 38-year-old was believed to be keen to assess the Brazilian’s mindset as he begins preparations for the opening Premier League match at home against Liverpool two weeks on Sunday. Although the former Al‑Ahli and RB Salzburg manager is still to be officially confirmed as Howe’s successor, Jaissle has been with his new squad since arriving in southern Spain on Saturday. Newcastle are waiting for the completion of some final paperwork before formalising his appointment.

One signing completed by Newcastle on Monday involved Lukas Hornicek’s £26m move from Braga. The 24-year-old Czechia goalkeeper is expected to replace Nick Pope as the team’s first choice, with Pope now likely to leave St James’ Park.

Hornicek caught Newcastle’s eye after seven clean sheets during Braga’s run to the Europa League semi-finals last season. At 6ft 6in, he cuts an imposing figure in goal and has been highly praised for the sort of high-calibre footwork that should improve Newcastle’s ability to play out from the back.

Hull had hoped to recruit Hornicek, but he turned down a move to the promoted club last month.

Sports.title: Transfer roundup: Chelsea sell Trevoh Chalobah and sign Jordan Henderson
Sports.content:
Trevoh Chalobah’s long association with Chelsea is to end after Como agreed a deal worth an initial £25.7m. The England defender’s departure was agreed on the same day the club completed the signing of Jordan Henderson.

Chalobah made 105 Premier League appearances for Chelsea and established himself as a first-team option during a number of turbulent periods for the club. The move will be seen as a coup for Como’s head coach, Cesc Fàbregas, with the former Chelsea midfielder pushing to bring the centre-back to Italy.

The clubs have settled on a package that includes £5.1m in performance-related add-ons and a sell-on clause. For Chelsea, the departure of another homegrown academy product – Chalobah, now 27, has been at the club since he was eight – will generate pure profit, a key factor as they continue to balance the books.

On another busy day in west London the new manager, Xabi Alonso, welcomed Henderson to the club after his departure from Brentford. The 36-year-old joined on a free transfer after playing 34 times for the Bees last season, a campaign that also earned him a place in England’s World Cup squad.

“Given the size of the club, the manager, who I have great admiration for, and the quality of the players, this was a huge opportunity I couldn’t turn down,” Henderson said. “I was so impressed with how much the ownership ‌want Chelsea to be successful and move in the right direction.”

View image in fullscreen With Jordan Henderson following Danny Welbeck to Chelsea, the club have shown a clear intent to sign more experienced players. Composite: Guardian Picture Desk

Henderson came through Sunderland’s academy before joining Liverpool in 2011. He spent 12 seasons at Anfield, playing 492 games in all competitions, and captained the team to Champions League victory in 2019 and the ‌Premier League title in 2020.

He left Liverpool for Al-Ettifaq in the Saudi Pro League in 2023, but ​six months later joined Ajax. He moved on again last summer to join Brentford.
