Henderson played six minutes at the World Cup before breaking an arm in a post-match accident after England’s last-16 victory against Mexico. He is Chelsea’s fourth English signing of the transfer window, after the record acquisition of Morgan Rogers ​from Aston Villa, Danny Welbeck from Brighton and the teenager Harrison Bettoni from Wigan.

Sports.title: Marc Skinner may have been a Marmite manager but Manchester United’s budget was spread thin | Tom Garry
Sports.content:
“If we want to compete at this later stage, we’ve seen what we’ve got to do, as a club. It’s our choice now, isn’t it? We have to look at what we seriously want to achieve … It takes, sometimes, a punch in the face to wake up.”

Those were the words of the Manchester United head coach Marc Skinner after his side went out of the Women’s Champions League with elimination by Bayern Munich in April. Just over four months later, the bruise from that punch has faded, but so, it would seem, have the club’s ambitions to compete in the transfer market, and Skinner has decided not to get into the ring for another round.

The 43-year-old wanted that run to the quarter-finals to trigger further investment in the starting team. The club, though, feel that the levels of spending in the transfer market are unsustainable and therefore want to focus on developing young, homegrown talent. Once that juxtaposition was firmly established this summer, it was inevitable that Skinner and United were likely to part company, as they did on Monday, to end his five years in charge.

United’s Marmite manager, Skinner certainly divided opinion in the WSL. He was the league’s longest-serving manager by a distance, but arguably also the most heavily maligned coach online. In the sport, though, there are coaches who admire the job he did on – according to the most recent set of WSL clubs’ financial accounts – a little over a third of the playing budget of Chelsea and around half that of Arsenal’s.

For members of the media, Skinner’s press conferences will probably be one of the most memorable aspects of his tenure, unique because of the extensive length of the former Birmingham and Orlando head coach’s answers. For example, before the 2025 Women’s FA Cup final, one of his answers was 1,000 words long.

View image in fullscreen Marc Skinner instructs his players in a Champions League tie against Brann in September 2025. Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/Reuters

To some, his determination to provide long, considered responses was a sign of his thoughtfulness and showed an admirable desire to be transparent. To others, his drawn-out answers demonstrated an inability to be concise and this communication problem dogged his relationship with the fans throughout much of his tenure. Often, unintentionally, his words would irritate sections of the fanbase. In 2025, one former United player privately described Skinner as a “great bloke, but he goes on a bit” and it is fair to say not every player liked his team-talk style, while others enjoyed his passion.

On the pitch, the 2022-23 season, Skinner’s second, was the club’s strongest as they finished second in the table, boosted by a robust defensive record, conceding 12 times in 22 games, and they came within a whisker of winning the title. Then there was the comparatively low moment of languishing down in fifth in the 2024-25 campaign, counteracted by winning 2025’s Women’s FA Cup, lifting United’s first major women’s trophy.

Yet, whether you loved him or loathed him at Leigh Sports Village, Skinner overachieved at United on a purely pound-for-pound basis, reaching four domestic cup finals – including three consecutive Women’s FA Cup finals – despite typically operating on a mid-table budget for much of his incumbency. He was certainly not every player’s cup of tea, and there will be lessons he will need to learn from the highs and lows of his five years at the club, but now that both of the coaches who have managed United’s women in the modern era have wanted to leave, in part, because of funding issues, there are questions for the club’s hierarchy to answer.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In the 2024-25 season, of the eight WSL clubs to publish their wage bills via Companies House, United’s ranked fourth for expenditure, and it was a similar story in 2023-24. For next season, they will operate on a far smaller wage bill than the big-spending independent club London City Lionesses and there are understood to be fears held among some staff at United that they are soon likely to be outbid for players’ wages by Tottenham too.

The club embarked on new direction this summer, establishing a long-term aim to sustainably succeed with young homegrown players and play exciting football in line with what they believe are the traditions of the club and their culture. Yet that seems to be at odds with the targets outlined during the 2024-25 season when their “Project 150” included a “Mission 1” for the women to win a first WSL title by the club’s 150th anniversary in 2028.

Whoever comes in as the club’s head coach – and an appointment is likely to happen quickly, with background checks having already been carried out on candidates – they will need to be prepared to work with youngsters and develop them rather than trying to sign established, international stars. They will also have to accept that key first-team players – such as Melvine Malard who was sold to Chelsea this summer – may well be poached by a rival.

Sports.title: Vinícius Júnior to Arsenal doesn’t make sense. That’s why it may work | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Sometimes what is needed is something different.

There is a long history in football of counterintuitive thinking being successful, of the benefits of creative tension, of adding grit to the oyster to generate the pearl, but even so, the news that talks between Vinícius Júnior and Arsenal on personal terms are progressing comes as something of a shock. Mikel Arteta’s great followers of a blueprint adding a free spirit like the Brazilian? Really?

Vinícius returns to Real Madrid this week after the World Cup with movement on his future expected relatively soon. He has 12 months remaining on his contract and Madrid are keen either to tie him down to a new deal or to sell him while he will attract at least some kind of fee. As their squad rebuild goes on under José Mourinho, Madrid’s position is readily understandable. They have already signed Bernardo Silva, Denzel Dumfries, Marc Cucurella and Ibrahima Konaté this summer; removing Vinícius’s £420,000 a week (about $30m/year) basic wages significantly increases their financial headroom.

There’s been a sense since Kylian Mbappé joined Madrid two years ago that having him and Vinícius together left the squad unbalanced. Why would you need two rapid forwards who both prefer to cut in from the left, particularly when Rodrygo, who tended to be consigned to the right before tearing his ACL in March, would also prefer to play from the left? Yan Diomandé is likely to confirm his move to Real Madrid from RB Leipzig this week. Although the Ivorian has said he would rather play on the right, he too has spent much of his career on the left.

More broadly, Vinícius does not seem a natural Mourinho player. His pace and technical excellence are undoubted, but he has never been the most diligent at fulfilling his defensive responsibilities. Mourinho likes a forward who can improvise, and worked successfully with Cristiano Ronaldo at Madrid, but it’s difficult to see how he could indulge more than one such player at a time, and Mbappé will take precedence.

But those concerns about tracking, about the willingness to stick to a gameplan, about the capacity to retain possession are just as relevant to Arteta as they are to Mourinho – arguably more so, as Arteta believes far more in structured attacking planning than Mourinho. Is Vinícius, after years of freedom at Madrid, really going to accept those rigid structures?

It’s been fairly clear since the second half of last season that Arsenal would be looking to strengthen their left side. The sale of Leandro Trossard to Beşiktaş did not come as a huge surprise. The 31-year-old is reliable and played a valuable role last season, starting 21 of the 38 league games and coming off the bench on a further 10 occasions, but there is not much stardust about him. Gabriel Martinelli started 11 league games and came off the bench 19 times, and his pace can be a great asset, but it’s no longer clear that he is at his best on the left. The signing of Eberechi Eze last summer looked like an attempt to add creativity from that flank but his tendency to drift infield when Arteta needs his left-sided forward to stay wide meant that by the end of the season he tended to be used centrally behind a striker.

Vinícius would give Arsenal greater attacking thrust. At his best, under Carlo Ancelotti, he could transform a game in seconds. His pace, dribbling ability and finishing mean that no matter how stale a game seems to have gone, no matter how under pressure his team may be, they are never more than seven or eight seconds from a potential goal. It’s easy to see why Arsenal are tempted by him. He would immediately be their highest-profile player, adding a sense of direction to a summer that, at least from a recruitment point of view, has seemed to be drifting. Arsenal missed out on Morgan Rogers, who joined Chelsea, while Julián Álvarez, who would seem a much more natural fit on the Arsenal left, appears more likely to go to Barcelona, if sufficient financial levers can be pulled.

But the fact Vinícius is not a natural fit may be part of the attraction. It was, after all, the season after signing Erling Haaland, far from a typical Pep Guardiola player, that Manchester City won the treble. A player who does not quite fit, who kicks against the general philosophy, can make a process team less predictable. The friction can produce valuable sparks.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Haaland, it’s fair to say, is a different personality from Vinícius and, as a center-forward, there was never a worry he was going to leave his full-back exposed. Vinícius is a bigger risk. He would certainly be an expensive one, not just in terms of his own salary but the inflationary pressure that could have on wages at the club more generally.

But he would also add a dash Arsenal have lacked that would make the accusation of being dead-ball plodders hard to sustain. And with Trossard gone, there is a left-sided hole that needs filling.

Sports.title: ‘They are terrified’: Como spark row with fans over controversial new stadium policy
Sports.content:
Como, the surprise package of last season’s Serie A, who qualified for the Champions League for the first time, will revoke season tickets from fans who fail to attend four home matches, under a series of new rules that have sparked a row among supporters.

The club, coached by the former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fàbregas, said on Monday that supporters “who miss more than three home matches without what it considers a valid reason risk having their season tickets revoked”. Another new rule bans fans from wearing the opposing team’s shirts or scarves anywhere in the stadium except the away section.

“Demand for tickets far exceeds supply and, for that reason, I asked the club to find ways to ensure tickets for the [Giuseppe Sinigaglia stadium] end up in the hands of genuine Como supporters – those who want to be there to back the team,” the chair, Mirwan Suwarso, said in a lengthy statement on Instagram.

“There have been too many occasions when away fans have celebrated inside our home sections, while Como supporters, who would have proudly backed the team, were unable to get a ticket.”

On the ban on wearing rival teams’ shirts, scarves and other symbols outside the away end, the club said the measure was introduced for safety reasons. “Our aim is to make the Sinigaglia the true home of our fans and a fortress for our team,” said Suwarso. “We want to ensure the Sinigaglia remains a place where grandparents feel comfortable bringing their grandchildren, where families can enjoy football together, and where passion never crosses the line into disrespect.”

On social media, many criticised the measures as overly harsh, arguing that work commitments, health issues or family responsibilities can prevent people from attending matches without making them any less loyal to the club.

La Provincia, Como’s local newspaper, said its newsroom had received dozens of calls and emails from concerned supporters. “Some worried about health problems or being unable to attend because of bad weather, as well as people who frequently travel for work,” the newspaper wrote. “They are terrified and all asking the same question: will our season tickets be taken away?”

Italy’s national newspaper, Corriere della Sera, reporting reactions from supporters on social media, quoted one fan asking: “Do we need to be accompanied by our parents when we hand in our excuse, like at school?”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In the 2018-19 season, Como were in Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football, after going bankrupt twice in the previous 15 years. Last season, the small northern Italian club finished fourth after an extraordinary campaign, producing a series of outstanding performances that surprised the football world.

Sports.title: Worn in the USA: Liverpool’s pre-season tour had highs but exposed glaring gaps in the squad | Andy Hunter
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola’s first pre-season tour as the Liverpool head coach produced wins over Sunderland in Nashville and Wrexham in New York before ending in a 4-2 defeat against Leeds in Chicago. The Guardian followed the tour throughout and here are a few things we learned.

Iraola’s vision will take time

Liverpool’s second-half display against Leeds was both concerning and valuable for the Iraola as set-piece problems and a tendency to switch off – two of last season’s recurring themes – reared their ugly head again, albeit after he had made changes. Liverpool’s opening 45 minutes, however, was their best of the tour and showed how effective his front-foot, more intense style can be with the big names back. But that process is only just under way.

Iraola is yet to even meet Virgil van Dijk, Cody Gakpo, Alisson, Alexis Mac Allister and new signing Víctor Muñoz since his appointment almost two months ago, never mind coach them. They will be finally acquainted when the squad reports back for training on Wednesday, having been given a little time off to recover from Sunday night’s flight from Chicago. Mac Allister will be still absent after his World Cup exertions. There is less than three weeks to go and only two more friendlies (although it is a double-header against Como at Anfield) before Liverpool open their Premier League season at Newcastle. “I would like to say on the first day we are going to be perfect, everyone will be in place,” Iraola said. “But probably it is not going to be like this.”

Head coach needs more backing

For most of the tour, Iraola was without eight first-team players due to World-Cup holidays and six because of injury, either recovering from or, as in the unfortunate Joe Gomez’s case, sustained in the US. No prizes for stating that Liverpool’s performances and adaptation to Iraola’s methods would have been much more advanced with 14 extra first-team players available. Even so, glaring gaps remain in the team when every option is taken into account.

View image in fullscreen Liverpool knew about Mohamed Salah’s departure months ago, but have yet to line up a replacement. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

Mohamed Salah’s departure was announced in March. Talks to end his contract one year early commenced earlier. Five months on from the announcement, he is yet to be replaced. The seriousness of Conor Bradley’s knee injury means Liverpool remain light at right-back. There are the highest hopes for Jérémy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni – the latter has transformed himself into a strapping Adonis while recovering from an anterior cruciate ligament injury, by the way – while 18-year-olds Ifeanyi Ndukwe and Mor Talla Ndiaye did well in the US. But Liverpool are lacking Premier League experience in central defence and Ndukwe will be unable to play this season due to post-Brexit work permit difficulties. Gomez’s injury record means he must be considered a bonus when fit, rather than one of four options. It was interesting to hear Iraola explain how he likes wingers to play both flanks, and the advantages of switching them during a game, but Liverpool’s right side could be a problem even if they succeed in signing Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain.

View image in fullscreen Trey Nyoni’s confident and assured displays pressed his case for more Liverpool game time. Photograph: Kamil Krzaczyński/AFP/Getty Images

Nyoni is now firmly in Iraola’s plans

There was an enforced reliance on young players during the tour and Iraola was genuinely impressed by the levels many showed in training and the friendlies. Ndukwe and Talla Ndiaye, as mentioned, Lewis Koumas, Kieran Morrison and Luke Chambers were among them. But no prospect pushed their first team claims further than Trey Nyoni, who grew in stature and confidence with every outing. The 19-year-old and Rio Ngumoha were permanent fixtures in Arne Slot’s squad last season, but while the winger made 19 appearances in the Premier League, including five starts, Nyoni had to settle for six league outings from the bench. On this evidence, there will be many more this season. The midfielder looked immediately at ease with Iraola’s instructions to find forward options as quickly as possible and did so whether under pressure or by creating space for himself with intelligent movement. His pass in the buildup to Florian Wirtz’s goal against Leeds was exquisite and in keeping with his contribution overall. Nyoni said after the Leeds game he knew he had to improve this summer. He was as good as his word.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Jones did not seize chance

To pinch a phrase from Salah, Curtis Jones looked more out than in at times as he enters the final 12 months of his Liverpool contract with increasing interest from the Italian champions, Inter. Unlike Nyoni and Dominik Szoboszlai, the 25-year-old did not adapt comfortably to Iraola’s requirements for a central midfielder and particularly struggled when introduced in the second half against Leeds. But it was his petulant reaction to not receiving the captain’s armband from Szoboszlai against Wrexham that did him fewest favours.

Jones was also overlooked for the captaincy when Gomez exited the opening game against Sunderland. On both occasions the armband was passed to Kostas Tsimikas, a reserve left-back who spent last season on loan at Roma. Of course, that was going to annoy a boyhood Liverpool fan and one of the more senior players on the tour, and Jones, Szoboszlai and Tsimikas all went to great lengths to laugh off the incident in the days after the Wrexham win. The row might have been overblown on social media, but given Iraola stresses the importance of the collective, Jones’s individualistic behaviour jarred with what he is trying to build.

View image in fullscreen Dominik Szoboszlai led the way for Liverpool on the US tour. Photograph: Daniel Bartel/Getty Images

Szoboszlai wins popularity contest

In the absence of Salah, Andy Robertson, Van Dijk and Alisson, and in keeping with his status as Liverpool’s player of last season, Szoboszlai was undoubtedly the big attraction for fans in the US. The Hungary captain’s every introduction and contribution was met with fanatical acclaim and his was the face the media wanted on their channels. More importantly for Iraola, Szoboszlai led the way in training and his leadership was invaluable given the relative inexperience of the squad. Fresh from signing a new five-year contract, the 25-year-old is an obvious choice to fill one of the vice-captain vacancies created by the departures of Salah and Robertson.

Sports.title: Why is the Carabao Cup first round being played over the weekend?
Sports.content:
Why is the Carabao Cup first round being played over the weekend?

The 2026/27 season will begin with the Carabao Cup on Thursday and run over the weekend after a major change was made by the EFL.

Following an exciting summer of World Cup football, the return of domestic competition is getting ever closer.



2 The Carabao Cup, won by Man City last season, is getting started this week Credit: Getty

And the Carabao Cup is always one of the first competitions on the calendar - but not usually the very first...

Typically, it would be the EFL kicking things off, with Championship, League One and League Two fixtures scheduled.

However, they won't be happening for another week and instead, it's the first round of the cup that begins the campaign.



Why is the Carabao Cup first round being played over the weekend?

The Carabao Cup first round was officially moved to the weekend commencing August 7-9 in January.

It was announced that, following consultation with clubs, rather than having the cup games in midweek following the league season's opener, they would be taking place over a weekend instead.



That represented a huge change made by the EFL, considering the Carabao Cup is traditionally always played in midweek.

The switch also means that players have more rest at the start of the season, having a week's break between games, rather than playing three matches during the first week of the campaign.



The statement released at the start of 2026 read: "The EFL start dates for the 2026/27 season have been confirmed, with Round One of the Carabao Cup set to kick off the new campaign, before the Sky Bet Championship, Sky Bet League One and Sky Bet League Two begin the following weekend.

"The 2026/27 season will see Round One of the Carabao Cup take place over the weekend of 7-9 August, with the League action set to start a week later over the weekend of 14-16 August."

So, the first round fixtures take place this weekend - and in fact, the season opener between Bristol City and Walsall is being played on Thursday night having been moved earlier due to a bizarre reason.

2 The EFL made a major change to the schedule to start the season with the cup competition Credit: Getty



Carabao Cup live on talkSPORT

talkSPORT will be bang across all of the action as the 2026/27 campaign officially gets going.

You can follow the first round of the Carabao Cup on talkSPORT, starting with Middlesbrough vs Wrexham on Friday.

Commentary of the clash will come from Mark Wilson and former Newcastle defender Steve Howey at 8pm.

There will also be live commentaries of West Ham vs Portsmouth, Colchester vs Southampton and Mansfield vs Sheffield United across the weekend.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app.

Sports.title: Tottenham tipped to sign Savinho and ‘vanilla bomba’ to conclude summer transfer haul
Sports.content:
Tottenham tipped to sign Savinho and ‘vanilla bomba’ to conclude summer transfer haul

Tottenham Hotspur have been tipped to wrap up their bust summer transfer window with two further attacking additions.

This was suggested on Inside Spurs, with the panel hesitant about whether Roberto De Zerbi's 'bomba' signing will be as exciting as first billed.

4 Spurs have been active in the summer transfer market, making Sandro Tonali their club-record signing Credit: Tottenham Hotspur FC

4 Tonali arrived just days after Mateus Fernandes completed his £85million switch across the capital Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Spurs have been incredibly active in the transfer market following their brush with relegation last season.

The north London side finished two points clear of the bottom three and only secured their top-flight safety on the final day of the campaign.

As such, Spurs have strengthened at the back and in midfield, including twice breaking their club-record transfer to initially sign Mateus Fernandes and then Sandro Tonali from West Ham and Newcastle, respectively.

Attention now turns to the attack, and De Zerbi hinted that a 'bomba' was imminent during the club's pre-season tour of New Zealand and Australia.

The Italian clarified his comments, but supporters still believe that a 'bomba' will be dropped before long.

Who is Spurs' next 'bomba' going to be?

And Snelling expects two more attacking players to come in before the transfer window closes next month, though one of the proposed additions hardly sets the pulses racing.

On the latest episode of Inside Spurs, Majestic enquired about the mystery 'bomba' and posed the question: "Who do you think it is?"

To which Snelling replied: "Well, this is the thing. Everyone's saying: 'Will it be Savinho?'

"But to me, a 'bomba' is something that comes out of nowhere. Like a shock. Like: 'Oh my god, who is this!?'

"To me, it probably will be Cody Gakpo. I feel like that is the one.

4 Savinho has been heavily linked with a move to Tottenham over the last 12 months Credit: Getty

"I can't see Spurs going all out and getting some world-class player at this stage.

"I feel like they'll get Savinho and Gakpo, and that will be all of the business done."

'It's a vanilla 'bomba'

Snelling, though, believes Spurs should avoid signing both forwards, continuing: "Personally, I would sign one of the two.

"I'm still undecided who I think of the two because they're two completely different players.

"I'd say Gakpo is more of your like goalscorer if you want to call him that, and Savinho is more of a creative type.

"But to me, I've said it on here a few times, it would be one of them, then you sign a world-class striker.

4 Gakpo would be a "vanilla 'bomba'" according to the Inside Spurs panel Credit: Getty

"But the market's tough for strikers and maybe this is what we have to do to just get by."

Summers echoed Snelling's sentiments, adding: "Neither set my world on fire in all honesty."

"It's a vanilla 'bomba', that's what it is. Not a chocolate 'bomba'," Snelling said of Gakpo links.

"Yeah, it's a light 'bomba'," Summers agreed.

Sports.title: Ex-Manchester United assistant Rene Meulensteen joins EFL club in newly-created role
Sports.content:
League One side Stockport County have announced the appointment of Rene Meulensteen in a newly-created role.

The Hatters confirmed the Dutchman's arrival as the Director of Football Methodology on Monday.

3 Stockport County created a role specially for Rene Meulensteen Credit: Getty

"Stockport County is delighted to announce the appointment of Rene Meulensteen as the club’s new Director of Football Methodology," a statement read on the club's official website.

"The vastly experienced Dutch coach arrives at Edgeley Park having spent more than two decades working at the highest level of the game, including an immensely successful spell at Manchester United under Sir Alex Ferguson."

"I’m delighted to be joining Stockport County as Director of Football Methodology," Meulensteen said later on Monday.

"It’s a fantastic opportunity to help build on the club’s progress and support the development of players, staff, and a clear football identity.

Meulensteen joins having last served as Graham Arnold's assistant manager for the Iraq national team between 2018 and 2024.

The appointment comes after a period of change off the pitch for Stockport.

Dave Challinor departed as manager following their League One play-off defeat to Bolton Wanderers earlier in the year.

Chief Executive Simon Wilson also left, and were replaced by Jim McNulty and Damien Allen, respectively.

McNulty admitted he is looking forward to working with Meulensteen, stating: "It is a genuine pleasure to be adding a coach of Rene Meulensteen’s calibre to our coaching team.

"Having operated at the very highest level, guided elite players, and gained invaluable experience across diverse footballing cultures in both domestic leagues and major international tournaments, he brings a tremendous breadth of wisdom and perspective to our coaching team.

3 It's been all-change off the pitch for Stockport County this summer

"This brilliant addition adds another layer of strength to our coaching collective and I am delighted Rene has decided to join our County team."

Allen, meanwhile, said: "Today marks a significant milestone in our club's history with the appointment of our first-ever Director of Football Methodology.

"His landmark appointment reflects our commitment to building an elite football department, where every player and coach across the club is aligned behind a clear football philosophy, coaching methodology, identity and way of working.

"We are delighted to welcome Rene to the club. His wealth of experience, football knowledge and proven success at the highest level will bring invaluable expertise to our coaching department.

"He will work closely with our first-team staff throughout the training week and on matchdays, while playing a pivotal role in the development of our football programme across the academy and first team.

Who is Rene Meulensteen?

The 62-year-old is best remembered for his time on the Manchester United coaching staff.

With Sir Alex Ferguson at the helm and the Dutchman part of the backroom set-up, United won the Premier League three times and the Champions League once before departing Old Trafford in 2013 after David Moyes took charge.

3 Meulensteen was briefly in charge of Fulham

Meulensteen briefly managed Anzhi Makhachkala, following up his stint in Russia with the role of Fulham boss in November 2013.

However, he was relieved of his duties in February 2014 as Felix Magath took charge at Craven Cottage.

Meulensteen returned to management in 2016 with Israeli outfit Maccabi Haifa and then on to Indian side Kerala Blasters in 2017 before taking up his position as Arnold's assistant for Iraq.

Sports.title: Liverpool need Trent Alexander-Arnold, he will unlock struggling star’s potential
Sports.content:
Trent Alexander-Arnold is the perfect player to unlock Liverpool's club-record signing Alexander Isak.

That's the opinion of talkSPORT pundit Gabby Agbonlahor amid talk of a potentially controversial return to Anfield for the right-back.

3 Alexander-Arnold contentiously left Liverpool for Real Madrid on a free last summer Credit: Getty

Alexander-Arnold contentiously left Liverpool for Real Madrid last summer, departing his boyhood club for the La Liga giants on a free transfer.

The English right-back, who was overlooked by Thomas Tuchel for the 2026 World Cup, endured a disappointing debut campaign in Spain as he managed just 14 league starts in an injury-hit season.

The addition of Dutchman Denzel Dumfries may further limit the 27-year-old's game time under Jose Mourinho in the upcoming campaign.

In the same transfer window Alexander-Arnold signed for Madrid, Isak completed his Premier League record transfer to Anfield, though the Swedish hitman struggled in his debut campaign on Merseyside, scoring just four goals for the club so far.

Liverpool 'need' Trent

And Agbonlahor believes that the best way for Liverpool to maximise Isak's talent is to bring Alexander-Arnold back to the Reds.

Speaking with Ade Oladipo on Drive, the former Aston Villa star said: "What's crazy is when you look at Liverpool now, they need him.

"They need Trent more than they needed him before. Because now, yes, [Sadio] Mane, and [Mohamed] Salah, and [Roberto] Firmino did start to get in the box maybe. But you've got your number nine, your focal point now, no Salah anymore."

Liverpool signed Jeremie Frimpong from Bayer Leverkusen last year to replace Alexander-Arnold.

Agbonlahor, though, believes that the Dutchman's skill set doesn't match what Liverpool need, continuing: "Isak is the main guy. What does he need? Great delivery. He's not going to get that from [Jeremie] Frimpong.

3 Agbonlahor criticised Frimpong on Drive on Monday

"Frimpong's a wing-back who's quick and he can get past a couple of players.

"He can't defend. I've seen him defend one v one, can't defend. His final ball is horrendous.

"So even like Isak's probably thinking I need some better delivery from that right hand side."

'I'll take him back'

Presenter and Liverpool fan Oladipo was asked whether he'd welcome Trent back given the manner of which he left, as he said: "I'll take him back...

"I'll take him back because the options at right-back are so bad. If Conor Bradley was fit, I'd say, give Conor another go.

"I don't think Frimpong's going to work. No. I always feel like that's an exercise that hasn't worked.

"Everyone should move on from it. He's not a right winger. He's not a full-back. I mean, he didn't get in the Dutch squad for the World Cup.

3 Alexander-Arnold has played 354 games for Liverpool... so far

"And that's not the best of squads. So that's not going to work. And Conor's always injured. I'll take him back."

Agbonlahor and Oladipo's comments come after Andros Townsend suggested that Liverpool 'should not turn their nose up' at the chance to bring Alexander-Arnold back to the club.

Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, Townsend said: "He doesn't need another season like he had last time.

"That would have been a big disappointment to him. Secretly, he would have been a little hurt that it never happened, he never really got going and had a few injury issues.

"I think Liverpool should, if they can get any deal done for him on a loan basis for a season, whatever those fees are now, up to £10million for a season, I wouldn't turn your nose up at that to get that boy back through the door.

"He is top, top drawer."

Sports.title: Aleksander Ceferin wants Club World Cup boycott as he plots Gianni Infantino downfall with Nasser Al-Khelaifi talks
Sports.content:
UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin is planning face-to-face talks with Nasser Al-Khelaifi at the Super Cup final on August 12.

Al-Khelaifi is one of Ceferin’s key allies and talkSPORT understands the UEFA President is pushing for European Football Clubs (EFC), chaired by Al-Khelaifi, to boycott the 2029 Club World Cup.



4 The walls are closing in on FIFA president Gianni Infantino with a potential Club World Cup boycott after a UEFA World Cup boycott last week Credit: Getty

However, this would require club-wide engagement with the 850+ members. Ceferin has made no secret of his own opposition to the Club World Cup, calling it a 'selfish endeavour' by Infantino back in May 2018.

The inaugural 32-team edition was won by Chelsea last summer, but plans for the 2029 event remain complete up in the air. No location or financing has yet been determined, and it is not covered by any current FIFA/EFC agreement.

Infantino has been hoping to expand the tournament to 48 teams, as well as launch a women's edition. The EFC was broadly supportive of the 2025 plans despite tensions in the lead-up to the tournament, and Al-Khelaifi played a pivotal role in determining the funding model.



Yet a major sticking point is promised solidarity payments from the 2025 edition have not yet been settled with many clubs demanding payment from FIFA.

The proposed 2029 Club World Cup lacks key foundational elements such as a location, funding structure, format or sponsors, and the tournament would not gain EFC support unless that changes.



Ceferin, meanwhile, wants the EFC to go public saying they will no longer work with FIFA on the Club World Cup while Infantino remains in charge.

UEFA are mobilising on a concerted effort for Infantino to resign. Ceferin has led calls for a blanket withdraw of letters in support of Infantino, and on Monday the Welsh FA confirmed they had revoked their endorsement pointing towards "recent failures in good governance, processes, leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgement."



The English FA are yet to release a statement, but talkSPORT understands they will also remove their support of Infantino.

Who wants to be president?

Ceferin himself has no plans to stand for FIFA president, but would support Al-Khelaifi doing so. The two will meet during the showpiece Super Cup clash between PSG and Aston Villa.

4 Ceferin is furious with Infantino but has no plans to stand against him

In fact, several UEFA Member Associations would back the Qatari executive to go head-to-head against Infantino even though sources close to the PSG president has 'no ambition' to do so, according to a a spokesperson.



There is a growing sense within UEFA that it might be better to back a candidate from outside the confederation in order to gain more votes. UEFA vice-president Laura McAllister told Hawksbee & Jacobs Infantino needs a rival if he doesn't quit.

"I think there has to be a candidate against Infantino now, and the important thing is that candidate can unite the opposition to him across the world," said the former Wales international.

"Clearly we have made our voice heard, as have the Asian federation (AFC) and Concacaf, but we need to have a candidate that can really unite the world to ensure he or she is capable of beating Infantino."

Concacaf president Victor Montagliani is giving serious thought to standing, and his confederation carries a further 35 votes. Alignment between UEFA and Concacaf could take a candidate to a maximum 90 votes, needing just 16 more for a majority.



However, Switzerland released a statement saying they want a 'personal exchange' with Infantino before determining next steps, while Czech Republic FA President David Trunda initially backed Infantino's controversial privatisation plans, even though UEFA's subsequent statement against FIFA Forward Enterprise made it clear all 55 members were opposed.

4 Al-Khelaifi is well thought of by Ceferin and other figures in European football but does not want Infantino's job Credit: Getty

Many insiders believe both Infantino and Montagliani are currently doing the maths to inform their position, but Ceferin is now hoping to either persuade Al-Khelaifi to stand or to get behind Montagliani.

UEFA insiders want a singular candidate to come forward believing it will encourage other federations to back them publicly.



talkSPORT can also reveal there are calls from some senior leaders for the remit and title of the FIFA president to be changed entirely into more of a ‘chair’ role.

This would see an elected official supported by a small inner circle of vice-chairs, representative of various bodies, that collectively report into the FIFA Council thus creating more checks and balances.

It would essentially found an executive leadership team rather than a sole leader. That could be a way of convincing Al-Khelaifi, as well as some high-profile confederation heads, to be back this proposal and even be involved

Infantino is also in many ways already campaigning having personally reached out to several federations. Saudi Arabia and Qatar were two of the first to back him, showing Asia, a key battleground, is not as united in its position as UEFA.



4 The World Cup proved to be something of a circus at points Credit: Getty

Bangladesh, Morocco, Kuwait, UAE, Bhutan and Sri Lanka are other federations to issue statements of support. It is clear Infantino hasn't lost much, if any, support in Africa.

The challenge for Infantino is even with these federations on side, UEFA now intend to bring FIFA into logistical and commercial gridlock, including a proposed Club World Cup boycott.

And Infantino must also deal with a divided leadership team, with several figures close to him wanting him to resign rather than faces months of instability.



Ceferin will hope by the time the Super Cup arrives, Infantino has already been persuaded to quit.

But those close to the Infantino are adamant it is not in his nature to stand down, and that his ability to pull off a 2026 World Cup that, as the FIFA President put it, 'destroyed all records' and needed 'new words to define the success' will keep a base of support – as will his ability to provide increased funding to member federations.

talkSPORT has contacted FIFA for comment.

Sports.title: Wrexham agree deal to sign captain of rival Championship club
Sports.content:
Wrexham have agreed a £3million deal to sign Preston captain Ben Whiteman, talkSPORT understands.

The midfielder has permission to undergo a medical ahead of his switch to the Welsh club.



3 Wrexham are closing in on their second summer signing in Whiteman Credit: Getty

Whiteman will bring an end to his five-and-a-half year spell at Deepdale in a move which represents a coup for Wrexham.

The 30-year-old has been captain of Preston for two years with Paul Heckingbottom's side coming 14th in the Championship last season.

Bad blood

Safe to say that Whiteman won't be wished well by Heckingbottom, who accused the player of 'crossing the line' in his bid to make the move.



"Ben told me, told Peter (Ridsdale, CEO) he's played his last game for the club," Heckingbottom said to BBC Radio Lancashire after a pre-season friendly against Stockport over the weekend.

"He's trying to force a move, which is an issue for me, for the players."



Heckingbottom added: "We've been in regular conversations in the last few days, and Ben knew there was a line I didn't want him to cross. Unfortunately he has, and you can't have that.

"My priority now is the players that are here and the players who want to play for us, and represent the club.



"Also Craig (Hemmings, owner) will have an issue with that, and Peter, because they pay the wages and things.

3 Heckingbottom didn't hold back in explaining how he felt Whiteman handled things Credit: Getty

"Listen, there's a valuation on him. I just hope for Ben's sake that Wrexham are willing to pay it, otherwise he's put himself in a really sticky situation."

Wrex appeal

But with an impending move to North Wales, Whiteman could be looking at Premier League football for the first time in his career.



Phil Parkinson's men narrowly missed out on the play-offs last season as they came seventh in the table.

They finished two points behind sixth placed Hull City, who went on to earn the final promotion spot into the top flight with a 1-0 win over Middlesbrough at Wembley.

Wrexham's promotion setback last term halted what has been a memorable run up the leagues which saw them go from National League to Championship in a remarkable three successive promotions.

They are of course backed by Hollywood actors Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney, who haven't been afraid to flex their financial muscles since purchasing their stakes in the club in 2020.



3 Parkinson took over as Wrexham boss in 2021, dragging them out of non league and potentially to the big time Credit: Getty

This summer has seen Wrexham make one notable signing so far with right-back Danny Imray arriving from Crystal Palace.

Meanwhile, several players have since left the club, including the likes of Paul Mullin, Jay Rodriguez and Andy Cannon.

Speaking on Wrexham's transfer business, Parkinson told talkSPORT last month: "I think last year we put 14 players in.



"You bring the players in different stages of pre-season. Some deals take longer than others, people moving into the area and it took us a while to find our feet in the division and also, I had players adapting to that.

"But I feel we've got a better, stronger squad in this pre-season and it's been great to work with the group so far, which we put together last season.

"However, I don't feel we're there yet in terms of the squad. We're not resting on our laurels and thinking, we're seventh and we're just going to naturally progress above that."

Parkinson continued: "You've got to be patient in your recruitment, but we still need to strengthen the squad for me to get a real feeling of confidence that we're ready to go and take it a step further.



"But we've got some good players and we were close. It's a very exciting season because it's going to be as competitive as ever."

Sports.title: Frank Lampard ‘one of the best in the world’ as Coventry prepare for ‘baptism of fire’ in Premier League return
Sports.content:
Frank Lampard ‘one of the best in the world’ as Coventry prepare for ‘baptism of fire’ in Premier League return

Frank Lampard has been named as one of the world's best coaches by Coventry City captain Matt Grimes.

The Sky Blues midfielder also called upon their supporters to revel in the upcoming season as they prepare for their Premier League return.

4 Lampard is held in high regard by all those associated with Coventry, especially Grimes Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Coventry made their way back into the top flight after a 25-year exile when they won the 2025/26 Championship title in April.

Lampard joined the club 17 months earlier with relegation a concern. However, he nearly achieved promotion in his first season, only to lose to Sunderland in the play-offs.

But he later went a step further and is a Premier League manager yet again after stints at Everton and his beloved Chelsea.

Grimes has spent a season-and-a-half at Coventry under the Blues legend, who he believes is up there with some of the very best in the management game.

In an exclusive interview with talkSPORT, the club skipper revealed: "I spoke to him on the phone before coming here, and the way he sold the project was a big incentive to come.

"Obviously, you want to learn from the best coaches in world - I believe he is that, and he was one of the best players in the world as well.

"All the knowledge he has, you try and soak in on a day-to-day basis. He's a pleasure to work with, you can see he's got the absolute maximum out of this group.

"We're ready to follow him now into the Premier League."

The champions? Bring it on

Last month, Coventry learned that they would face Premier League holders Arsenal in the opening match of the new season.

The Friday night fixture, which will be live and exclusive on talkSPORT, will come at the Emirates Stadium on August 21.

4 Coventry are back amongst the top 20 sides in the country Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

4 A huge test at Arsenal awaits them on the opening weekend Credit: Getty

Arsenal will arrive on their home turf brimming with confidence that they can make a winning start to their title defence.

However, Grimes and his teammates are relishing the challenge that awaits them in 18 days' time.

"It doesn't get much more difficult than the champions away from home," he said. "We're looking forward to it, it's a bit of a baptism of fire to be honest.

"But you want to test yourself against the best, and that's as difficult a task as you're going to get in the Premier League this season.

"We'll make sure we're ready for it."

Coventry 'back where they belong'

Relegation from the Premier League in 2001 came amid reported debts of £60million at Coventry.

4 Coventry are ready and raring to go for their first Premier League game in 25 years Credit: Getty

They sold their former ground Highfield Road two years earlier and began work on their new home, the Coventry Building Society Arena.

Arena Coventry Limited (ACL), a partnership of Coventry City Council and The Alan Edward Higgs Charity, first owned the stadium.

However, the Sky Blues were involved in a row over rent and had to play the 2012/13 season at Sixfields, home of Northampton Town.

They then played at Birmingham City's ground of St Andrew's for two seasons after failing to agree a deal with rugby side Wasps.

Finally, Coventry returned to their home in 2021 and, four years later, bought it from the Mike Ashley-led Frasers Group.

Now that they are back in the big time, the future looks bright, and Grimes has called upon supporters to soak it all in next season.

"Just enjoy it," he said. "We've been through so much, or, you guys have been through so much for so many years. We're back where we belong, go and enjoy it.

"Enjoy every game no matter the result, no matter the situation. Just take as much from it as you can."

Sports.title: EFL club to receive second transfer fee for player sold earlier this summer in bizarre twist
Sports.content:
EFL club to receive second transfer fee for player sold earlier this summer in bizarre twist

Leicester could receive a second transfer fee for Bilal El Khannouss this summer, just months after the Moroccan's departure.

Attacking midfielder El Khannouss completed a permanent move to Bundesliga sideStuttgart in May, having spent the 2025/26 campaign on loan from the Foxes.



4 El Khannouss was a mainstay in a successful 2025/26 campaign for VfB Stuttgart Credit: Getty

The Morocco international joined the German side last summer following Leicester's relegation from the Premier League.

His initial loan move included an option to buy, which was subject to appearances, and Stuttgart announced in May that they had activated this option.

Reports in Germany claim Stuttgart paid around €17million (£14.6m), on top of the £2.6m loan fee they paid last year, to sign El Khannouss.



It was also reported that Leicester had a sell-on clause in the transfer, which they could now be set to benefit from earlier than expected.

Not another one?

According to Sky Germany's Florian Plettenberg, El Khannouss is open to leaving Stuttgart, just over two months after his permanent arrival.



While the Bundesliga outfit are keen to keep hold of the 22-year-old, they are likely to demand a substantial fee should he depart.

Plettenberg reports that the Swabians could slap a €60m (£51.3m) asking price on El Khannouss, as well as bonuses.



While the playmaker's interested parties are not currently clear, two Premier League clubs are rumoured to have made initial enquiries.

Should a move materialise, El Khannouss could make a return to English football less than a year after his initial departure from Leicester.

He joined the Foxes in 2024 from Belgian side Genk, and made 39 appearances, scoring three goals and providing seven assists in his debut season.

4 El Khannouss was a shining light in a bleak 2024/25 campaign for Leicester Credit: Getty



4 New Leicester boss Russell Martin would welcome any sell-on fee if the Moroccan moves club again this summer Credit: Getty

But with the 2016 English champions suffering relegation to the Championship, El Khannouss was allowed to depart on loan at the start of the 2025/26 campaign.

Any prospect of him returning this summer then became unlikely after Leicester were relegated again in April, this time to League One.

The Foxes are now bidding to bounce back to the second tier at the first time of asking, with new manager Russell Martin tasked with overseeing their promotion charge.



Busy summer

Having already earned a substantial figure from El Khannouss' permanent exit, Leicester would no doubt welcome an additional fee for him in the same transfer window.

Reported Premier League interest in the creative star comes after he featured six times for Morocco at the World Cup in North America.

El Khannouss started in all of his country's games as they were ultimately knocked out in the quarter-finals by France.

4 El Khannouss has earned 43 caps for Morocco, six of which came at the 2026 World Cup Credit: Getty



This was his second World Cup campaign, having also been part of the Morocco squad that reached the semi-finals in 2022.

Prior to this summer, El Khannouss made 39 appearances in all competitions for Stuttgart.

He scored nine goals and registered a further nine assists to help his side to a fourth-place Bundesliga finish and secure Champions League qualification.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes confirms arrival in La Manga as Newcastle REJECT Arsenal bid, Chelsea agree £26m deal to sell Trevoh Chalobah to Como... and Preston skipper is set for controversial £3m exit to Wrexham: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Fulham snap up Real Madrid star

Fulham have confirmed the £36m signing of striker Gonzalo Garcia from Real Madrid.

The 22-year-old has signed a five-year deal with the option to extend by a further 12 months.

'I'm very grateful, very happy to be here', he told the club website.

Fulham have confirmed the £36m signing of striker Gonzalo Garcia from Real Madrid

'I have to thank the board and Arbeloa for the trust they've put in me, and I'm very, very excited to start.'

West Ham in market for Spurs outcast

West Ham are among the clubs interested in signing Manor Solomon from Tottenham, as first reported in Window Watch last week.

Solomon has impressed Roberto de Zerbi during a pre season tour of New Zealand and Australia.

De Zerbi knows the Israel international well because they worked together at Shakhtar Donetsk but the winger is set to leave after failing to hold down a place in three years at Spurs.

At 27, he is only interested in a permanent move, having spent last season on loan at Villarreal and Fiorentina and the previous season on loan at Leeds, where he sparkled as they won promotion from the Championship to the Premier League.

Fiorentina retain an interest despite not taking up the option on a permanent deal after his loan.

West Ham are among the clubs interested in signing Manor Solomon from Tottenham

Others are also monitoring the situation, and Spurs have to sell players to clear space in De Zerbi's squad and generate more income.

West Ham are in the market for a winger after selling Crysencio Summerville, but captain Jarrod Bowen has committed his future to the Hammers despite relegation.

MATT BARLOW

Preston boss hits out with Whiteman set for exit to Wrexham

Preston North End have accepted a £3million bid from Wrexham for their wantaway captain Ben Whiteman.

Manager Paul Heckingbottom voiced his displeasure at the weekend, saying Whiteman had crossed a line after telling them he had played his last game for the club in an effort to force through the move.

'Ben knew there was a line I didn't want him to cross and unfortunately he has,' Heckingbottom told BBC Radio Lancashire. 'There's a valuation on him, I just hope for Ben's sake that Wrexham are willing to pay it otherwise he's put himself in a sticky situation. He's made his bed. I'm not bothered as long as I get another player.'

The 30-year-old midfielder is now free to have a medical and complete the transfer, with personal terms not expected to be a problem.

The deal is expected to go through in the next 48 hours and Preston are looking to reinvest the money in another three or four new signings this summer.

Paul Heckingbottom says Ben Whiteman has 'crossed a line' in making his move

Hammers plot £18m bid to land Parrott

West Ham are preparing to outbid European rivals to sign former Tottenham striker Troy Parrott.

The Hammers want to bolster their attack quickly with the new Championship season looming and after being rebuffed for Sunderland's Wilson Isidor, are targeting AZ Alkmaar forward Parrott.

The Republic of Ireland international has interest from Ajax, Como, PSV Eindhoven and Real Betis but Alkmaar are reluctant to sell to a Dutch rival.

The Hammers hope an offer of around £18million will be enough to fend off the competition.

Parrott struggled while at Spurs but after an initial loan to Excelsior Rotterdam he began to find his feet and has been prolific with Alkmaar since.

Troy Parrott celebrates winning the Johan Cruyff Shield with Alkmaar on Sunday

Henderson's relish as he joins Chelsea

Chelsea have announced the signing of 36-year-old Jordan Henderson, after he was allowed to leave Brentford with a year left on his deal.

'Given the size of the club, the manager, who I have great admiration for, and the quality of the players, this was a huge opportunity I couldn't turn down,' Henderson said.

'I was also so impressed with how much the ownership want Chelsea to be successful and move in the right direction.

For more on this story click HERE

Jordan Henderson signs on the dotted line as he joins Xabi Alonso's Chelsea revolution

Sunderland block the door to Isidor

West Ham have asked to take Sunderland winger Simon Adingra on loan, but the Wearsiders have no plans to sell forward Wilson Isidor.

West Ham have asked about both players but after initial conversations Sunderland have made it clear that they want to keep Haiti international Isidor.

Discussions are ongoing between the clubs over a straight loan for 24-year-old Ivory Coast international Adingra.

Despite interest from a host of clubs, however, Sunderland will not entertain offers for Isidor. The 25-year-old remains an integral part of their squad ahead of their season in European competition and the club believe he can build on an excellent World Cup with Haiti.

West Ham are continuing to discuss AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott while Lazio are interested in the Hammers' German international forward Niclas Fullkrug.

Wilson Isidor is back after the World Cup and Sunderland say he is not for sale despite interest

Como agree £26m Chalobah deal... as Napoli eye Badiashile

Chelsea and Como have agreed a £26million fee for defender Trevoh Chalobah.

The deal will include a further £5.2m in add-ons for the 27-year-old England centre-back who is expected to travel to Italy on Wednesday evening.

Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile continues to attract interest from Napoli. The Blues are looking to recoup funds for the French centre-back as well as for Axel Disasi who has been the subject of talks with Crystal Palace and West Ham - both are discussing offers.

Disasi had a spell on loan at West Ham last season but ideally wants a top flight offer.

Chelsea hope to make progress with Rayo Vallecano over the purchase of left wing-back Pep Chavarria.

Trevoh Chalobah is on his way to Como, managed by former Blues star Cesc Fabregas

Newcastle reject Arsenal bid for Bruno as he joins Magpies in La Manga

Arsenal's opening bid for Bruno Guimaraes has been rejected by Newcastle. As reported earlier, the clubs are now in direct talks over a deal for Brazilian.

Guimaraes has landed in Spain and is travelling to report back for Newcastle's pre-season camp in La Manga today.

Newcastle's new manager Matthias Jaissle is at La Manga with the squad and wants to meet the captain.

Bruno Guimaraes is subject of interest from Arsenal but they have not yet made a formal offer

Guimaraes confirmed his arrival in Spain on Instagram on Monday evening

Bernardo gets shirty at Real

Bernardo Silva has arrived at Real Madrid as he joins up with Jose Mourinho's side. The 31-year-old left Manchester City at the end of last season.

The Portugal star, who has returned from the World Cup, was seen signing shirts for fans after medical tests.

🎥 @ainoafrndz pic.twitter.com/7wFAeRQm2F — Le Journal du Real (@lejournaldureal) August 3, 2026

Man United would loan out Chido Obi for game time

Manchester United are willing to send striker Chido Obi Martin out on loan this summer.

The 18-year-old Denmark U21 international had interest from Cologne earlier in the window, but they have moved to sign Jaiden Heskey from Manchester City and are lining up Tottenham winger Mikey Moore.

Chido Obi joined United from Arsenal's academy in 2024 and has made seven first-team appearances though failed to score.

United want to ensure his next club is one where he can develop properly with competitive game time.

Join the queue for Everton's Tim

Everton midfielder Tim Iroegbunam is attracting increasing interest from rival Premier League clubs and from abroad.

Coventry City, Hull City and Ipswich Town have all made enquiries while two Italian clubs have also asked about the 23-year-old.

Lazio tried to sign the former England U20 international in January.

Everton are continuing to discuss a deal for Arsenal's Christian Norgaard which, if completed, could pave the way for Iroegbunam to depart once a suitable offer comes in.

Everton paid around £9million to Aston Villa for Iroegbunam in 2024.

Tim Iroegbunam joined from Aston Villa two years ago

Coventry keen on Mudryk

Chelsea have received multiple approaches about Mykhailo Mudryk from clubs following the news of his return to football – including three from the Premier League.

Coventry City, managed by Frank Lampard, who worked with Mudryk at Stamford Bridge in 2023, are believed to be among those to have enquired, sources have told Daily Mail Sport.

All options are open between Mudryk and Chelsea this summer, including whether to send him out on loan after his sudden comeback from a doping suspension.
