Sports.title: Jordan Henderson's move to Chelsea confirmed: England midfielder, 36, joins Blues after ripping up Brentford contract
Sports.content:
Chelsea have confirmed their signing of Jordan Henderson on a free transfer, after Brentford allowed the 36-year-old to terminate his contract a year earlier than expected.

It comes two days after they secured the signature of Danny Welbeck, 35, from Brighton.

Between them, Henderson and Welbeck will add 863 Premier League games’ worth of experience to a changing room now overseen by new manager Xabi Alonso, 44.

Henderson said: 'Given the size of the club, the manager, who I have great admiration for, and the quality of the players, this was a huge opportunity I couldn’t turn down.

‘I was also so impressed with how much the ownership want Chelsea to be successful and move in the right direction.

‘For me, it's about giving everything every single day, both on and off the field, to help the players around me and the team as much as possible. I'm very excited to get going.’

Jordan Henderson's move to Chelsea has been confirmed after he ripped up his Brentford deal

The midfielder was all smiles as he spent the day at Chelsea's Cobham training ground

Henderson, 36, said he was ready to 'give everything every single day, on and off the field'

Alonso identified during his talks to take over Chelsea that their squad was in need of greater balance among the players. The Blues had broken Premier League records for fielding the youngest sides over the previous two seasons, but they had been criticised by fans on occasion for appearing to lack maturity on and off the pitch.

Chelsea previously targeted Granit Xhaka, the 33-year-old Sunderland captain who had worked with Alonso at Bayer Leverkusen, but were unable to get him out of the Stadium of Light. They likewise showed interest in John Stones, who has now joined Inter Milan at 32.

Yet they have now secured Henderson for free, while the fee for Welbeck is being described as ‘undisclosed’, though his cost is by no means substantial, if indeed there even is one.

Welbeck has already travelled to Hong Kong to join his new team-mates. Daily Mail Sport reported last week how Brentford were ready to sanction Henderson’s exit rather than seek a fee from Chelsea. He is still recovering from the broken arm he suffered with England at the World Cup.

These signings are concrete confirmation that Chelsea have adjusted their transfer strategy by now aiming to add experienced leaders to their squad. Previously, there had been a focus on finding younger players of potential.

Maxence Lacroix, 26 and from Crystal Palace, has already been confirmed by Chelsea for £52million. Morgan Rogers has also arrived for £117m from Aston Villa.

Sports.title: Aryna Sabalenka backs tennis' new transgender rules forcing stars to take mandatory sex tests as World No 1 says 'it's obvious men are biologically much stronger than women'
Sports.content:
Aryna Sabalenka backs tennis' new transgender rules forcing stars to take mandatory sex tests as World No 1 says 'it's obvious men are biologically much stronger than women'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Aryna Sabalenka has welcomed the Women's Tennis Association's (WTA) new transgender eligibility rules, insisting it is only fair for those competing in women's tennis.

Announced last month, the WTA has become the latest sporting organisation to implement genetic testing in a bid to establish players' eligibility to compete as a female.

The governing body's previous policy permitted biological males to compete in the women's category if they maintained testosterone levels below a certain level.

But now a tweak to the rules states that WTA players must undergo a sex screening for the SRY gene, which is found on the Y chromosome and is typically involved in male sex development.

Only once they have passed the test - which is completed through a simple cheek swab, blood test or saliva sample - will players be eligible to compete on the female-only WTA Tour.

A positive test, meanwhile, will spark further medical assessment before a player is cleared to play against their female rivals. Players must also sign documentation acknowledging that refusal to be tested could result in disciplinary action.

World No 1 Aryna Sabalenka has welcomed the WTA's new transgender eligibility rules

Last December, Sabalenka lost to Nick Kyrgios in a 'Battle of the Sexes' exhibition in Dubai

Speaking about the move, world No 1 Sabalenka was in favour of the changes and said she would have no hesitation in undergoing the testing herself.

'It's very important to maintain fairness in our circuit,' the 28-year-old said.

'It's obvious that, biologically, men are much stronger than women, so it wouldn't seem fair to me for a woman to compete against a biological man.

'I think it took them a while to make this decision and, yes, I support it.

'But I'm concentrating on myself, on my goals, on whatever it takes. If you want to test us all, I will gladly do so, it's pretty fair, and let's keep it that way.'

Last December, Sabalenka competed in a 'Battle of the Sexes' match with Nick Kyrgios which she lost 6-3, 6-3 in Dubai. That exhibition drew much criticism, with many brandishing it as a publicity stunt that risked trivialising the women's game.

Sabalenka isn't alone in her thinking about the new WTA transgender rules, with tennis icon Martina Navratilova - who has been strong in her views on keeping trans athletes out of women's sport - quick to praise the WTA for making the move last month.

Writing on X, she said it was a 'step in the right direction', adding: 'I played no part in this particular policy, but am very happy that we at the WTA are clear that we are a women's association and only women, as in females, can compete at the highest level of women's tennis.'

Martina Navratilova (right, with the Princess of Wales at Wimbledon) has praised the policy

Other organisations, such as World Boxing and World Athletics, have already implemented similar testing for their athletes seeking to compete in the women's category.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) has also confirmed it will sex test athletes ahead of the next Olympic Games, which will be held in Los Angeles in 2028.

Sports.title: Match delayed by PARROT attack: Incredible moment Brazilian youth game is stopped as bird swoops down on player
Sports.content:
A Brazilian youth game was bizarrely halted at the weekend when a parrot attacked a player.

Flamengo were taking on Ceara in the Brazil Under 15 Cup on Saturday, but the match took an unusual turn just 17 minutes into the first half.

As one Flamengo defender attempted to pass the ball to a team-mate, a blue-and-yellow parrot swooped down towards him, forcing the player to dive to the floor in panic.

The bird then appeared set to go for another player until it flew away at the last moment.

It went on to pester several other players, causing the referee to pause the game, before it eventually flew off.

However, it returned about 25 minutes later when it came down and perched on the pitch, leading to another stoppage.

Parrot ATTACKS soccer player during match between youth teams in Brazil



It definitely bet on the opposing team to win pic.twitter.com/AQ8799Owf3 — RTVisual (@RT_Visual_on_X) August 3, 2026

A Brazilian youth game was bizarrely halted at the weekend when a parrot attacked a player

The parrot went on to pester several other players and caused two stoppages in the match

The bird was later identified as a blue and yellow macaw, a parrot that is typically found in the tropical rainforests of South America.

Flamengo went 1-0 up in the match, but, perhaps impacted by the stoppages, suffered a 2-1 defeat.

The parrot intervention is unusual, but not new, with an amateur game in Turkey between Istanbul Yurdum and Mevlanakapi Guzelhisar halted earlier this year when a seagull was hit by the ball.

The bird dropped to the ground and players rushed to its aid, with the Istanbul captain Gani Catan seen giving CPR to it.

Catan later carried the seagull to the side of the pitch where it received further medical treatment.

Sports.title: World Cup final villain Leandro Paredes sparks another on-pitch melee just weeks after Spain antics - as Argentina thug is booked for classless act
Sports.content:
Leandro Paredes was back antagonising opponents on a football pitch at the weekend with some of his antics, but this time at club level.

Paredes' spoiling tactics caught the eye for the wrong reasons last month during Argentina's World Cup semi-final win over England and even more so during his country's abject final defeat by Spain.

He has since returned to club action and played for Boca Juniors in their 2-2 draw at Newell's Old Boys on Sunday in the Argentine Primera Division - Torneo Clausura.

And during that encounter, the 32-year-old was back producing some 'dark arts' with one particular flashpoint.

Trailing 2-1 to the hosts, Paredes started an on-pitch melee when he appeared to deliberately kick a ball at a stricken opponent on 68 minutes.

As the player, who had just been fouled, was returning to his feet and with his back turned, Paredes booted the ball at him.

After controversy at the World Cup, Leandro Paredes has found himself in hot water again 😬 pic.twitter.com/vGSMmG0eRL — Match of the Day (@BBCMOTD) August 3, 2026

Leandro Paredes sparked a melee during Boca Juniors' 2-2 draw at Newell's Old Boys

Paredes appeared to kick a ball deliberately at a stricken opponent during Sunday's encounter

The 32-year-old's actions saw him booked as he was confronted by Newell's Old Boys players

Paredes threw Spain's Gavi to the floor in disgraceful scenes after the World Cup final in July

The act saw angry players from Newell's Old Boys confront him before the referee brandished him a yellow card for his act.

This latest act follows Paredes' shameful post-match actions after the World Cup final when he bizarrely fought some members of Spain's victorious team.

He grabbed defender Eric Garcia by the neck, pushed over Gavi and also appeared to throw punches after Argentina's defeat. He was also fortunate not to be sent off towards the end of normal time for a foul.

FIFA has since launched disciplinary proceedings against Paredes for the unsavoury scenes - he faces three counts of assault as well as a charge of unsporting behaviour.

Sports.title: England's World Cup nemesis Valentin Barco joins Chelsea: Argentina star who provoked Three Lions in semi-final defeat confirms switch to Stamford Bridge after Atlanta antics
Sports.content:
Chelsea have confirmed the signing of World Cup villain Valentin Barco on a seven-year deal.

Barco, 22, who can play in midfield and at left-back, joins the Blues from their sister club Strasbourg.

The Argentine hit the headlines last month when he clashed with Jude Bellingham after England's semi-final defeat at the World Cup.

Barco made just one substitute appearance at the tournament, but he infuriated the Three Lions after he sprinted across the pitch when Enzo Fernandez equalised late on in the clash.

He ran right in front of several England players and appeared to taunt them, before John Stones reacted by giving him a shove.

Barco later also came onto the pitch in the aftermath of Lautaro Martinez's winning goal.

Chelsea have confirmed the signing of World Cup villain Valentin Barco on a seven-year deal

Barco clashed with Jude Bellingham after Argentina's semi-final victory over England

There were also reports that the new Chelsea star had been winding up the England bench for the entirety of the 90 minutes.

In response to his antics, Bellingham gave the 22-year-old a slap on the back of the head after the full-time whistle as Argentina's players celebrated, causing a scuffle on the pitch.

Given his involvement in the World Cup, Barco won't join up with his new team-mates until later in pre-season.

The versatile star began his career back home with Boca Juniors, making his debut at the age of 16.

After impressing in Argentina, Barco joined Brighton in 2024 for £7.4million yet he struggled to establish himself on the south coast, and spent time on loan at Sevilla and Strasbourg.

He joined Strasbourg permanently in July 2025 and was regularly linked with a move away after impressing in France, where his side qualified for Europe.

Barco contributed 12 goals and assists last season and his strong form saw him earn a place in Argentina's World Cup squad, although he played just 19 minutes in a group stage victory over Jordan.

Bellingham slapped Barco on the back of the head following his overzealous celebrations

His arrival at Stamford Bridge comes following the exit of Marc Cucurella to Real Madrid, although Chelsea are still in negotiations with Rayo Vallecano for left wing-back Pep Chavarria after making an improved offer.

Barco is the Blues' seventh signing of the summer, with Danny Welbeck, Morgan Rogers, Maxence Lacroix, Geovany Quenda, Marco Palestra and former Strasbourg striker Emmanuel Emegha all also joining the club.

He has similarly become the 13th player to move between the French side and Chelsea since BlueCo took over Strasbourg in 2023, a year after they purchased the Premier League side.

Sports.title: Who will win the 2026 Ballon d'Or? Bookies reveal clear favourite as Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi seek prestigious honour - but will one of Spain's World Cup heroes take the prize?
Sports.content:
With the World Cup having concluded, Harry Kane, Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal will be among the stars with their sights set on football's ultimate personal accolade, the Ballon d’Or.

Performances of several stars at the tournament have furthered their claims for the honour, with several Spain stars surging up the list of favourites after playing key roles in their triumph.

The Ballon d'Or will officially be announced on October 26.

Will there be a repeat winner or will a new name be on the honour roll for the third consecutive year?

Daily Mail Sport takes a look at the possible contenders to receive the prestigious prize.

Ousmane Dembele won last year's Ballon d'Or and is among the contenders again for the award

Harry Kane – 1/1

Heading up this list of possible winners is England captain and Bayern Munich’s No9, Harry Kane.

Kane has been at the peak of the footballing world for over a decade now, but has a serious chance of becoming the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the Ballon d'Or after the best statistical season of his career.

The 33-year-old scored a staggering 61 goals in 51 matches last season for Bayern Munich to help the German giants achieve a domestic double, as well as reaching a Champions League semi-final.

Despite Bayern falling to PSG in the last four, Kane scored in both legs of the semi-final, as he had also done against Real Madrid in the previous round.

Kane was equally brilliant for England in the World Cup, having been instrumental as Thomas Tuchel's side progressed to the semi-finals.

The England captain scored six goals, including two braces, but his lack of involvement in their semi-final loss to Argentina could count against him.

Historically just two domestic trophies would not be enough to win the Ballon d’Or but Kane’s mind-boggling output over the past year means he remains the bookies' favourite to win the prestigious prize.

Harry Kane could become the first English player to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen

Lamine Yamal – 9/4

Kane will have his work cut out for him though, as the second on the list of favourites for this year’s award is Lamine Yamal.

The Barcelona and Spain star is seen as having a strong chance to become the first teenager to win the Ballon d’Or.

Since the start of last season, Yamal has been simply unstoppable. The Spaniard enjoyed a stellar season for both club and country, winning La Liga, the Spanish Super Cup and of course the World Cup.

Yamal racked up an impressive 16 goals and 12 assists in 28 La Liga games, while he also netted six times and assisted four goals in the Champions League.

His contribution would have likely been even higher had Yamal not seen the end of his season blighted by injury. He made a speedy recovery in time for the World Cup and while he may have not been at his blistering best, the winger played a vital role.

The 19-year-old, who started all but one game, was crucial to Spain’s success, despite only scoring one goal.

The threat he posed forced teams to double up on him, providing open space for teammates. Yamal was also expert in drawing free kicks and penalties through his trickery. Even with a low output his effect was still felt.

Spain's World Cup success has boosted Lamine Yamal's chances following on from his stunning season with Barcelona

Rodri – 9/2

Spain's World Cup winning captain Rodri has emerged as a leading contender following the tournament.

Rodri is an interesting case amongst this year’s favourites and presents the voters with a dilemma.

To many captaining your side to a World Cup with eight flawless performances should immediately make you a top candidate for the honour, but Rodri’s year has been disrupted by several injuries, preventing him from playing half of the Premier League season.

When on the pitch Rodri has been outstanding and he was deservedly named as the World Cup's Player of The Tournament after orchestrating sublime victories over France and Argentina in the semi-final and final respectively.

Victory for Rodri would indicate that performances in the biggest games are key, rather than consistency over the course of 12 months.

Rodri's starring role for Spain at the World Cup has pushed him into contention for the honour

The Spain captain was named as the World Cup's best player after their final triumph

Kylian Mbappe – 6/1

While French superstar Mbappe went another season without a trophy, his individual performances and numbers have been typically magnificent over the past nine months.

With Real Madrid, Mbappe netted an impressive 42 goals in 44 games, including 15 in 11 Champions League outings to end as the top scorer in the competition.

Mbappe was undoubtedly one of the leading figures at the World Cup, scoring ten goals to win the golden boot, finishing clear of his nearest challenger Lionel Messi.

The haul also saw Mbappe become the outright leading goalscorer in World Cup history.

Despite Mbappe reiterating his individual brilliance once again, a lack of silverware may hold him back from winning his first Ballon d’Or.

Kylian Mbappe secured the golden boot at the World Cup, but a lack of silverware my hold him back

Lionel Messi – 8/1

The timeless talent of Messi never seems to fade.

Messi, viewed by many as the greatest of all time, showed us this summer that he is far from finished and remains decisive on the world stage.

Despite Argentina losing the final, Messi's World Cup performances alone could bring him an extraordinary ninth Ballon d’Or.

Messi silenced doubters from the first match, in which he scored a hat-trick against Algeria. He would go on to contribute goals and assists in all but one of Argentina’s World Cup matches, racking up eight and four respectively.

While it may not hold as much weight as European domestic success, in late 2025 Messi spearheaded Inter Miami to their first ever MLS Cup victory, scoring six goals and getting seven assists in just six MLS play-off games.

Despite his advancing years, Messi was the inspiration behind Argentina's path to the World Cup final

Ousmane Dembele – 12/1

Reigning Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembele is in contention for back-to-back triumphs.

After years of ridicule and derision in the early 2020s, Dembele has been transformed from an underachieving talent to the world’s best under Luis Enrique at PSG.

For the second year running, Dembele won the Champions League with the French side. The forward held his nerve to score their all-important equaliser from the penalty spot in the final against Arsenal – his 20th goal of the season.

Dembele also enjoyed a prolific World Cup with the Frenchman scoring six goals, including an excellent hat-trick against Norway. But his lack of influence in helping Les Bleus past Spain in their semi-final may count against him.

Ousmane Dembele helped PSG retain the Champions League, putting him in contention for back-to-back Ballon d'Or triumphs

Jude Bellingham – 14/1

Bellingham’s reputation was already stellar before this year, but he became England's Birmingham Baggio as he attempted to drive the Three Lions to the World Cup final, akin to how the ponytailed star had done for Italy in the 1994 tournament.

Similarly to his Madrid teammate Kylian Mbappe, Bellingham failed to pick up any silverware and will be massively held back by that in the voting. However, it would be ignorant to not at least consider Bellingham for the prize.

The midfielder certainly possesses the talent to deserve the prestigious award. However, the award rarely goes to the most gifted footballer at the time, but rather the most successful in that year’s campaign.

So unfortunately for Bellingham, despite his heroic England performances and unquestionable quality, a season in which you win no silverware and register 13 goals and assists in 40 games is unlikely to cut it.

Jude Bellingham starred for England at the World Cup to put him in contention for the award

Pau Cubarsi and Fabian Ruiz – 16/1 and 18/1

Two Spain stars from their World Cup triumph are viewed as outsiders for the prize.

Teenager defender Cubarsi was named as the Best Young Player at the World Cup, with Spain having conceded just one goal on their route to winning the tournament.

Cubarsi is joined by midfielder Fabian Ruiz, who has won both the World Cup and Champions League this year.

Despite getting fewer than ten goals and assists across the club season and the World Cup, Ruiz's contribution to his club and country’s success through his ability to keep and advance possession amongst other abilities has been invaluable.

Pau Cubarsi was named as the best young player at the World Cup after starring in defence for Spain

Fabian Ruiz won both the World Cup with Spain and the Champions League with PSG

Luis de la Fuente's decision to start him over Pedri in the latter stages of the World Cup and the performances that followed or his ability to stand out in a midfield with Joao Neves and Vitinha is a testament to his place in this list.

As across 1,131 minutes in Ligue one this past season Ruiz maintained a 91.5 per cent passing accuracy rate, was in the 99th percentile for progressive passes completed and the 82nd percentile for both key passes and chances created to other midfielders.

These performances alongside his trophy haul for the season make the Spaniard an outside shout for the award.

Sports.title: Emma Raducanu is OUT of the US Open: British tennis star's horror run of injuries continues as doctors advise former champion to skip New York - hours after releasing video training in protective boot
Sports.content:
Emma Raducanu will miss the US Open as she continues to recover from the stress fracture which forced her to pull out of Wimbledon on the eve of the Championships.

It is a continuation of the British No1's dreadful run of injury and illness and - given the Open is the final Grand Slam of the year - her season is in danger of petering out.

The 23-year-old has been in St Moritz, Switzerland, from where she posted a video of herself practicing serves - with the significant caveat that she was still wearing a protective boot on her right leg.

And Daily Mail Sport understands that after her latest medical checks, the British No1 has been advised that the injury needs more time to heal and so she will be unable to contest the final Grand Slam of the season.

This latest issue is a continuation of a theme - since she won the US Open Raducanu has rarely been able to stay fit for a sustained period.

The lower-leg stress fracture - which first came to light when she was spotted leaving the All England Club in a protective boot in the week before Wimbledon - came on the back of a viral illness which laid her low for much of February through until May.

Emma Raducanu is set to miss the US Open later this month as her injury woes continue

The British No 1 had earlier shared a photo of her practicing in an orthopedic boot on Monday

Raducanu has been spending some of her rehab time in the high luxury of the Suvretta House hotel.

Opened in 1912 in the mountains of St Moritz, rooms can cost up to £2,500 a night.

The five-star hotel has a picturesque clay tennis court - upon which, it appears, Raducanu was unable to do much more than serving off one leg.

British tennis fans who follow and support Raducanu are used to disappointment but this recent run of illness and injury is particularly maddening given how well she has played during her brief periods of health.

In Cluj, Romania, and at the Queen's Club this year she made her first finals since the US Open title in 2021.

And her promising reunion with Andrew Richardson, the man who coached her to that miraculous Grand Slam title, is stuck in the starting blocks.

As ever, Raducanu's talent and athletic ability mean she is still capable of great things if she can stay fit. The problem is, with each passing year that 'if' becomes ever bigger.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn makes seven-figure demand for latest star but admits he 'might not be the best'
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn makes seven-figure demand for latest star but admits he 'might not be the best'

England and Northampton star Henry Pollock is now managed by Matchroom and Eddie Hearn - who is seeking a record pay day for the player's next contract

View 2 Images Eddie Hearn is handling Henry Pollock's contract talks

Eddie Hearn has claimed that Northampton star Henry Pollock is "a seven-figure player" as he goes into contract talks with Northampton - even if the promoter admits "there might be players who are better".

‌



Pollock opted to join up with the Matchroom supremo several months ago and now has Hearn leading his contract negotiations with the Prem champions. The 21-year-old’s contract is thought to be around £150,000 per year, but it expires at the end of next season.

‌



Hearn is looking to land the England back rower a bumper pay day and has told Northampton to "recognise what they have got" whilst he stated that Pollock was "making an unquestionable difference to the bottom line of the club."

‌



The Matchroom chief is a hugely influential figure and has talked up the money Pollock could get if he chose to move elsewhere - and his financial demands would make Pollock comfortably the highest paid player at Franklin's Gardens.

Lewis Moody health latest as star arrives at Wimbledon after MND diagnosis READ MORE :

England strategy in the spotlight as Prem's best leaves and Exeter boss spells out reality READ MORE :

Hearn told the Telegraph: “It is all very well saying that there might be players who are a bit more consistent or might be better or whatever, but there aren’t players that are making an unquestionable and undeniable difference to the bottom line of the club.

‌



“Henry Pollock drives season ticket sales. Henry Pollock puts bums on the seats. Henry Pollock drives viewership on TNT or wherever it’s going to be. Henry Pollock sells shirts, right? That’s the difference. So you can actually put an economic value over having Henry Pollock on the team, and that has to be recognised, regardless of the want from Henry. He cannot stay at this club on the money that he’s on.”

Alongside his Northampton contract Pollock also receives around £150,000 per year from the Rugby Football Union as an enhanced elite player squad member with England. Northampton though have spent under the £6.4m cap with their marquee player thought to be fly-half Fin Smith.

View 2 Images Henry Pollock was recently with Eddie Hearn on his yacht (Image: @henryjpollock)

Article continues below

Reports claim Tommy Freeman will soon pen a deal that makes him the Prem's best paid winger but Hearn has talked up Pollock's financial pull off the pitch, even if the player would like to remain at Northampton. He also claimed the club's opening offer was not a “fair representation of his commercial value”.

“The first thing I said to Henry was: ‘Do you want to stay at Northampton?’” Hearn said. “And he said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘I love the club, I love the team, I love that I live 10 minutes away, and I think we’re going to win the championship again next year and I want to win championships'."

If Pollock wants to remain playing for England, which is the case, then he will have to sign with a club in the Prem. Many of those are already spending close to the cap and few would have the scope to pay a player £1m as things stand.

Sports.title: Emma Raducanu OUT of US Open as injury nightmare continues for British No.1
Sports.content:
Emma Raducanu OUT of US Open as injury nightmare continues for British No.1

Emma Raducanu has been forced to skip the US Open due to a stress fracture in her lower right leg, having missed Wimbledon earlier in the summer

View 2 Images Emma Raducanu has been hampered by injuries recently (Image: Getty)

Emma Raducanu will miss a second consecutive Grand Slam tournament as she continues to recover from a stress fracture in her lower right leg.

‌



The world No. 49 is set to skip the US Open after pulling out of Wimbledon on the eve of the tournament earlier this summer.

‌



Raducanu, 23, has not played a match since finishing runner-up at the Queen’s Club almost two months ago. It’s now been five years since the Brit made history at the US Open, becoming the first and only qualifier to win a Major title.

‌



But on the half-decade anniversary of her heroic run, she will not compete in Flushing Meadows.

The US Open gets underway in less than four weeks, but Raducanu has already decided to skip the event on medical advice and is said to be sad to miss such a special tournament.

Since pulling out of Wimbledon, the British No. 1 has been spotted wearing a protective boot on her right leg. She has also shared footage from some early practice sessions. One video showed Raducanu sitting on a bin and hitting balls. In a second clip, filmed during a trip to Switzerland, she stood on a clay court and hit some serves.

‌



The US Open concludes on September 13, by which time Raducanu won’t have played a match for three months. She was also not named in Britain’s squad for the Billie Jean King Finals, which takes place in Shenzhen from September 22 to 27.

View 2 Images Emma Raducanu withdrew from Wimbledon less than 24 hours before her first round match (Image: Getty)

The world No. 49 also missed more than two months of competition from March to May due to post-viral illness, while a bone bruising injury in her foot wrecked her pre-season preparations. And the stress fracture is the latest issue to derail Raducanu’s 2026 season.

Article continues below

Announcing her withdrawal from Wimbledon on the night before her first-round match this summer, she said: “I can’t believe I’m saying this, but sadly I’ve had to withdraw from this year’s Wimbledon.

“I’ve done everything possible to try to get to the start line tomorrow but after a final scan tonight, the niggle I’ve been managing has developed into a stress fracture and I’ve been medically advised to stop pushing through.

“Playing at Wimbledon, in front of a home crowd, means everything to me, so this is really difficult to process. I want to thank you all for your support and encouragement. Especially at a time like this, it is invaluable. I look forward to seeing you when I’m back.”

Sports.title: Southampton boss Tonda Eckert says he received death threats after Spygate scandal
Sports.content:
Southampton boss Tonda Eckert says he received death threats after Spygate scandal

Tonda Eckert became public enemy number one after authorising a junior Southampton staff member to spy on opponents' training sessions last season

View 2 Images Tonda Eckert remains in charge of Southampton (Image: Matt Watson/Southampton FC via Getty Images)

Tonda Eckert says he received death threats and was told by the police not to drive anymore following the Southampton Spygate scandal.

‌



Southampton were kicked out of the Championship play-off final after admitting they spied on rival clubs. They will start the 2026/27 season on -4 points, while Eckert is still awaiting the outcome of a Football Association charge.

‌



The German coach is at the centre of things, after the FA determined the spying on Oxford United, Ipswich and Middlesbrough was a "contrived and determined plan from the top down".

‌



Saints' hierarchy have stuck by Eckert, who remains in charge despite the possibility he could be handed a lengthy touchline ban. The 33-year-old says he was sent supportive messages from "well-known colleagues" in both England and Germany, but the reaction from the public was intense.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Asked if he received death threats, Eckert told Kicker: "Yes, it could no longer be handled without the police. I do not want to go into details, only this much: I was advised not to drive myself any more, but to sit in the back of the car instead. That was very difficult."

‌



He added: "It was a situation no coaching course prepares you for. No training explains how to react when, for security reasons, you are suddenly supposed to sit in the back seat. As I said, it was very difficult."

The FA charged Eckert with acting in an improper manner, or bringing the game into disrepute. He has been overseeing pre-season preparations in Germany, with Saints targeting promotion back to the Premier League once more, and admits the charge hanging over his head has complicated things.

"I would be lying if I said that it is not in the back of my mind," Eckert told BBC Radio Solent. "I think that's true for everyone involved, but the positive thing is I just love the game. I love football - there's so much to prepare for.

‌



View 2 Images Tonda Eckert could still be banned for Spygate (Image: Trevor Wilkinson/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

"There's so many things to do in the pre-season with training preparation and a transfer window, and once you lock into whatever is needed at the very moment, that's all that matters.

"It's not that it's constantly on my mind but obviously we'll be happy when the decision comes at one point and until then I just keep my head down, working, and I think the boys are in a good place."

‌



Eckert has insisted he didn't know the EFL rules banning the observation of opponents' training sessions, which he says is common practice in other countries.

"It's tough to read some of the things that are out there, I've held my hand up for this judgement on something I have authorised," he previously told BBC Radio Solent.

"I am responsible and I apologise for bad judgement; we've be in now for a week and there comes a point to look forward and from the first day back in, there's been lots of smiles and a good energy in the place again."

Sports.title: Man Utd ready to battle Barcelona for £13.7m star as they establish transfer plan B
Sports.content:
Man Utd ready to battle Barcelona for £13.7m star as they establish transfer plan B

Manchester United are looking to make additions at left-back and, should they miss out on Newcastle's Lewis Hall, then they could battle Barcelona for Spanish teenager Jorge Salinas

View 2 Images Man Utd have been keeping tabs on highly rated Spanish teenager Jorge Salinas

Manchester United are reportedly considering a move for Racing Santander full-back Jorge Salinas, who is their back-up option should they miss out on Lewis Hall.

‌



The Newcastle star is on the club's shortlist and the Magpies have already seen a number of their leading lights leave this summer. Bruno Guimaraes is being pursued by Arsenal and could follow Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali out the door with the club into a period of transition.

‌



Eddie Howe has just called time on his five-year tenure and United are looking to seize on the uncertainty around the club by going after Hall, who has continued to blossom since moving to St James' Park from Chelsea.

‌



Newcastle are in no hurry to cash in on Hall and would demand an offer in excess of £50million before they even considered letting the England international leave - which has left United having to look elsewhere.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Alejandro Garnacho takes brutal swipe at Chelsea immediately after Aston Villa debut READ MORE :

And Spanish newspaper SPORT claim that Santander’s Salinas has emerged as a target. The club hold a genuine interest in the 19-year-old, but if he does move on then his preference is thought to be a move to Barcelona. He played a key role last season as his boyhood team won promotion to La Liga.

‌



As it stands the Red Devils are prepared to pay Salinas’ €16m (£13.7m) release clause, but it remains to be seen how willing the player himself is to make the move. Barcelona see Salinas as a replacement for Joao Cancelo, who is set to make the move to Saudi Pro League outfit Al-Hilal.

United have been keeping close tabs on Salinas and were impressed by his performances at this summer’s European Under-19 Championship, where Spain claimed the trophy.

View 2 Images Lewis Hall has been heavily linked with Man Utd (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Article continues below

United's first choice left-back is Luke Shaw and the ex-Southampton man has been an impressive and consistent performer, but fitness has been an issue throughout his career and the versatile defender is now 31.

Already this summer United have signed Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos with bolstering their midfield a priority for the Red Devils. They could yet add more quality in that area but left-back is also an area that had been cited as somewhere they could improve their squad.

Sports.title: Chelsea sign Jordan Henderson as ex-Liverpool captain completes shock move
Sports.content:
Chelsea sign Jordan Henderson as ex-Liverpool captain completes shock move

Former Liverpool midfielder Jordan Henderson has completed a move to Chelsea at the age of 36, having been allowed to leave Brentford for nothing midway through his contract

View 2 Images Jordan Henderson has left Brentford for Chelsea (Image: Chris Lee/Chelsea FC)

Chelsea have completed a deal to sign England international Jordan Henderson. The former Liverpool captain, 36, has signed a two-year deal at Stamford Bridge after leaving Brentford.

‌



Henderson still had another year left on his contract with the Bees but was allowed to leave for nothing. The addition of the former Liverpool star is intended to add more experience to a young Chelsea squad under Xabi Alonso, with ex-Manchester United and Arsenal forward Danny Welbeck, 35, also arriving on Saturday.

‌



The veteran duo have been joined at Chelsea this summer by the more youthful trio of Morgan Rogers (24), Marco Palestra (21) and Valentin Barco (22).

‌



"Given the size of the club, the manager, who I have great admiration for, and the quality of the players, this was a huge opportunity I couldn’t turn down," Henderson said.

Xabi Alonso drops telling hint over Chelsea’s Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck transfers READ MORE :

Chelsea hoping to repeat Man Utd and Liverpool's inspired transfer deals with latest moves READ MORE :

"I was also so impressed with how much the ownership want Chelsea to be successful and move in the right direction.

"For me, it's about giving everything every single day, both on and off the field, to help the players around me and the team as much as possible. I'm very excited to get going."

‌



View 2 Images Jordan Henderson has joined Chelsea after leaving Brentford (Image: Getty Images)

Henderson started his career with boyhood club Sunderland and moved to Liverpool in 2011. The midfielder made 492 appearances on Merseyside, helping the club to the Premier League and three Champions League finals, as well as a whole host of other trophies as captain.

He quit Anfield in 2023 in a move to Saudi Arabian side Al-Ettifaq but he was soon on the move once again with subsequent switches to Ajax and Brentford. His form last season was good enough to secure a spot in England’s squad for the World Cup.

Article continues below

The 93-capped midfielder made just one appearance at the tournament with a six-minute cameo against Panama in the Three Lions’ final group game. He suffered a horrendous arm injury after falling from the advertising hoardings around the pitch.

Sports.title: Saffie Osborne to captain Ryan Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle in Shergar Cup at Ascot
Sports.content:
Saffie Osborne to captain Ryan Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle in Shergar Cup at Ascot

The Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup at Ascot on Saturday has been boosted by the news that Ryan Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle will be in action

View 2 Images Saffie Osborne (centre) will lead a team featuring Dylan Browne McMonagle (left) and Ryan Moore (Image: PA)

Ryan Moore will make only his second appearance in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup at Ascot on Saturday, with the event further strengthened by confirmation that rising star Dylan Browne McMonagle will compete.

‌



Moore, who secured the Silver Saddle award for leading rider in the team competition during his only previous participation in 2006, has been freed up with no Flat racing scheduled in Ireland that afternoon.

‌



Moore and McMonagel will represent the Great Britain and Ireland team which will be captained by Saffie Osborne at the event which will also feature teams from Hong Kong, Europe and the Rest Of The World.

‌



The Hong Kong Jockey Club will field a team, led by Vincent Ho, who claimed Shergar Cup glory in 2019 as part of the victorious Rest of the World squad. He will be accompanied by Jerry Chau and Luke Ferraris.

Christophe Lemaire will skipper Europe, alongside Marie Velon and Frida Valle Skar, while Jamie Melham (nee Kah) will return to spearhead the Rest of the World. She will be partnered by Japan's Yutake Take and Suraj Narredu, who steered team Asia to victory last year.

‌



Ascot's head of corporate and industry affairs Will Aitkenhead said: "It's absolutely fantastic to have Ryan and Dylan on board. Both had very strong Royal Ascots, with Ryan the leading jockey, and both had very good weeks at Goodwood.

View 2 Images Jamie Kah: Melbourne Cup winner will ride at Shergar Cup (Image: Getty Images)

"It's really helpful the Phoenix Stakes has moved from the Saturday to the Sunday at the Curragh this year which frees them up and it's great to have them board.

Article continues below

"We'd been in discussions with Oisin (Murphy) and Billy (Loughnane) earlier in the year and they were keen, but they just don't know where they'll be. Obviously Hollie Doyle would have been here, but she's sadly injured.

"In previous years we've lined them up early which helps with the marketing and everything, but this year we were keen to get the strongest teams that we could so waiting until this week made sense."

On the subject of overseas riders, Aitkenhead commented: "Jamie Melham returns as a Melbourne Cup winner, she's huge in Australia and Yutake Take is the biggest name in Japan. We've got Christophe Lemaire and the Hong Kong team led by Vincent Ho as well so we've got some really strong teams."

Sports.title: Jockey allegedly headbutted official and told another ‘if you keep filming, I am going to slap you’
Sports.content:
Jockey allegedly headbutted official and told another ‘if you keep filming, I am going to slap you’

Jerome Claudic became aggressive and insulting after staff tried to stop him entering an area reserved for corporate guests at ParisLongchamp

View 3 Images Jerome Claudic (second right) was banned for one month (Image: Icon Sport via Getty Images)

A jockey allegedly headbutted an official and told another ‘if you keep filming, I am going to slap you’, according to a disciplinary inquiry.

‌



Jerome Claudic, a jockey with nearly 20 years experience, has ridden 27 winners in France this year and over 500 during the course of his career.

‌



He was reported to the France Galop stewards following an incident after racing at Paris Longchamp in July in a corporate hospitality where a garden furniture design business was entertaining guests. The disciplinary panel was told that Claudic, who appeared "heavily intoxicated", had attempted to enter the area with two female friends insisting he was entitled to be there.

‌



When challenged he unleashed “a torrent of insults” at France Galop and described the guests and partners as “buffoons”.

During a six minute outburst, which included racist comments, he was filmed by the company's head of digital who he ordered to put away her phone, telling her, "If you keep filming, I’m going to slap you". He then delivered a “completely unprovoked headbutt” to a member of France Galop staff, the hearing was told.

Claudic was escorted to the exit by a France Galop staff member but as he left uttered “death threats, threats of physical violence, and racist remarks—shouting, in particular, 'You two are dead men walking'.

‌



View 3 Images The incident occurred after racing at Longchamp (Image: Getty)

Claudic explained when interviewed that he had been looking for somewhere to watch the football. He admitted losing his temper when he saw someone filming him but denied headbutting anyone. He said he had been under the influence of alcohol after drinking a "small glass," but that he was mainly tired and annoyed by the video taken without his knowledge.

He explained that jockeys undergo gruelling work schedules, including in intense heat on that day, and he felt worn out.

‌



The panel was told: “He intends to go straight home after races from now on; he and his colleagues feel unwelcome at this racecourse—which provides no designated space for professionals—and since this has caused problems before, he will never set foot there again.”

He apologised and said he had never behaved in that way before and on that evening it was simply a case of having "had enough".

View 3 Images Claudic said jockeys don't feel welcome at Longchamp (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The France Galop stewards said Claudic had “displayed behavior that was absolutely intolerable and unacceptable. This conduct cannot be justified by the explanations he provided; while the apologies he offered must be taken into account, they do not absolve him of responsibility.”

The panel added his behaviour damaged “the image and reputation of the racing institution and the sport itself”.

It said it was also clear Claudic had not learned the lessons of previous disciplinary actions having previously been suspended for six months in 2021, following a test that revealed the presence of a narcotic substance.

Article continues below

Claudic was referred to the France Galop Medical Department for potential psychological, medical, and addiction-related follow-up. He was suspended from riding for one month with another three months suspended for five years.

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League star blocks £113m Real Madrid transfer as FIFA receive complaint
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League star blocks £113m Real Madrid transfer as FIFA receive complaint

Max Gradel, the ex-Bournemouth winger, has filed a complaint to FIFA that has thrown Yan Diomande's reported £113million move to Real Madrid into doubt

View 2 Images Real Madrid have reportedly agreed a deal to sign RB Leipzig star Yan Diomande (Image: (Photo by Stuart Franklin/Getty Images))

Former Premier League winger Max Gradel has filed a compliant to FIFA regarding Yan Diomande's proposed £113million move to Real Madrid.

‌



Diomande, 19, who is viewed as one of the most exciting attacking talents in world football, has agreed a club-record deal to join Jose Mourinho's Madrid side this summer. The Ivory Coast international netted 13 goals and added 10 assists in 36 matches for RB Leipzig last season and appears destined for Los Blancos.

‌



But the transfer has run into a major stumbling block due to a legal dispute over representation rights, according to AS and Defensa Central. Real Madrid struck the deal with Roc Nation, the sports agency founded by rapper and businessman Jay-Z, under the belief they were Diomande's sole representatives.

‌



Liverpool transfer need brutally exposed as Leeds stun Andoni Iraola - 5 talking points READ MORE :

Ex-Man Utd star tipped for bright future by Alex Ferguson speaks out on being clubless READ MORE :

However, Maxidel Management, headed up by ex-Bournemouth, Leeds United and Leicester City forward Gradel, have launched a lawsuit to FIFA alleging a breach of contract. Maxidel brokered Diomande's switch from Leganes to Leipzig last summer and maintain they hold his rights until he departs the German club.

The dispute has brought the deal to a grinding halt, despite Diomande previously being on the verge of putting pen to paper on a five-year contract at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Real Madrid are said to be absolutely furious over the situation, feeling misled by the lack of transparency throughout negotiations. Having reached a broad agreement with Roc Nation, the sudden emergence of Maxidel's claim has thrown serious complications into the mix.

‌



Ivorian journalist Malick Traore shed light on the club's frustrations, saying: "Real Madrid are angry with Diomande's representatives at Roc Nation, after discovering that the player is still tied to a contract with other agents."

View 2 Images Former Premier League star Max Gradel has put a halt on Yan Diomande's move to Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

The fury is aimed solely at Roc Nation, not at Diomande himself. Real Madrid now face a precarious predicament, as settling a commission with the incorrect agent could trigger severe sanctions from FIFA.

‌



Gradel, 38, started his senior career at Leicester and made his breakthrough during the Foxes' League One title-winning season in 2008/09, scoring some important goals including an equaliser in a 2-2 draw at MK Dons.

He went on to leave Leicester in 2009 and join Leeds on loan and then on a permanent deal. He played a pivotal role in propelling the Whites to promotion from League One before delivering the standout campaign of his career in the Championship, netting 18 times across 41 appearances.

That impressive spell secured him a transfer to Saint-Etienne in Ligue 1, where he remained for four seasons before heading back to England with a Premier League switch to Bournemouth. Gradel subsequently turned out for Toulouse, Sivasspor and Gaziantep before transitioning into life as a football agent.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Play-off Path A:

Semi-final: Italy vs Northern Ireland

Semi-final: Wales vs Bosnia and Herzegovina

Final: Wales/Bosnia and Herzegovina vs Italy/Northern Ireland - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off

Play-off Path B:
